actionable.title: Travel all can burn up to 60 days when the Navigator is vacant or keeps getting lost
actionable.description: travelAll loops up to 60 runDay() calls. It stops only on null, end of trip, a non-'nothing' encounter, or pace.blocked. A vacant Navigator fails automatically off-road (engine resolveDay: actorUuid null -> success false), so lost=true, moved=[], and the trip never ends. If the hex has no encounter table, or the table returns nothing, every one of the 60 iterations drains rations and water, pays wages, rolls wear on nothing, and advances world time by a day. Undo only restores the last day (ledger keeps one snapshot). Roles do not carry over from 0.1.x data (migrateCaravan only keeps saved.roles, which 0.1.x caravans did not have), so on a migrated world tonight every role starts vacant. The first Travel all on a road-less course would then spend 60 days of supplies and time, and Undo cannot fix it.
actionable.reason: In live play this destroys supplies and world time with no recovery path. The migration path makes it likely on first use.
actionable.suggested_fix: In travelAll, break when out.lost (or when no hex was moved), and/or refuse to run Travel all while the Navigator role is vacant. Alternatively, cap Travel all at the course's estimated days.
actionable.rationale:
80: I could not refute this finding. Every link in the chain checks out in the code, and the loop is new in this diff (travelAll was added in 912eaa4).

1. **The loop never sees the stall.** travelAll (src/travel/index.ts:342-353) runs up to 60 runDay() calls. It breaks only on four conditions: a null result, the trip ending, `lastEncounter`, or `out.pace.blocked`. Nothing checks `out.lost` or an empty `out.moved`.

2. **A vacant Navigator always fails off-road.** In src/engine/index.ts, resolveDay sets `success: false` when `actorUuid === null`. Only road hexes skip the check, because `auto` is set from `road`. That makes `lost = pv.moving && !ok("navigator")` true and `moved` empty. In the travel case, `lost` sets `done = false`, so the trip never ends. `pace.blocked` stays null because the caravan can still move; it just got lost.

3. **Each lost day still costs a full day.** runDay drains rations and water, pays wages, applies vehicle wear, increments journeyDay, advances world time by a day, and posts a chat card, all without making progress.

4. **The encounter break rarely fires.** DEFAULT_RULES has `encounterTable: null`, and `lastEncounter = !!table && !isNothing(text)`. A hex with no table can never stop the loop, and a table that returns nothing doesn't either.

5. **Undo restores only one day.** The comment in src/ledger/index.ts says each day's snapshot replaces the previous one, so only the last day can be undone.

6. **Migrated caravans start with every role vacant.** migrateCaravan (src/store/index.ts) keeps only `saved.roles` holders. The 0.1.x types have no per-caravan role holders, so `roles` comes out as `{}`. A fresh caravan with no Navigator assigned hits the same path.

There is one mitigation, which is why the score isn't higher. The trigger needs an off-road course, a vacant Navigator (or one who keeps failing), and the GM pressing Travel all. The per-day chat cards would announce "lost the way" each day, but the loop runs without stopping, so the GM can't step in. This is a real correctness bug that is likely in tonight's session.

actionable.title: GM choosing a hidden route in the Travel window silently clears the course
actionable.description: For the GM, the route <select> lists Object.values(view.routes), where view is the full map, so routes unknown to the party appear too. The change handler looks the chosen id up in store.partyView(...).routes, which only holds routes with knownToParty. For a hidden route, route is null, course is [], and setPlan posts 'cleared the road', wiping any existing plotted course.
actionable.reason: A GM action in live play destroys the plan with no feedback.
actionable.suggested_fix: Look the route up in the same map the select was built from (store.getMap for the GM, partyView for players), or list only known routes for everyone.
actionable.rationale:
80: I tried to refute this and could not. The bug is real, it is on lines this diff added, and it triggers through a normal GM action.

1. For the GM, src/ui/travel-app.ts:79 builds `view` from `store.getMap(...)`, which is the full map. Line 127 lists `Object.values(view.routes)` and filters only on `courseAlong(...).length`, not on `knownToParty`. So any hidden route through the caravan's hex shows up in the dropdown, with no marker saying it is hidden.

2. The change handler at line 164 (new in this diff) looks up the chosen id in `store.partyView(...).routes`. In src/store/index.ts:234-236, `partyView` copies a route only `if (route.knownToParty)`. A hidden route's id therefore returns `undefined`.

3. `route` is falsy, so `course = []` and `routeId = null`. The handler then calls `travel.setPlan(...)` with the message "cleared the road".

4. `setPlanHandler` (src/travel/index.ts:280-296) has nothing to stop it. It refuses only during a trip, for an unknown activity, or for an invalid course, and an empty course passes. It overwrites `after.plan` with an empty course and records "<GM> cleared the road" as the last edit.

How it triggers: the GM draws a route left hidden from players (`knownToParty` false), the caravan sits on one of its hexes, the GM opens Travel, and picks that route. Any course already plotted is wiped, and the dropdown goes back to "Follow a known road…" with no warning.

The old code (15741e7) used one `map` for both listing and lookup, so this mismatch is new. The only things that soften it are the visible "cleared the road" note and that the GM can plot the course again. The main risk is losing the plan without warning; the info-leak question doesn't arise, because only the GM can see hidden routes.

actionable.title: `publicRegion` returns neutral rule values that look real, so player previews show DCs that differ from what is rolled
actionable.description: `partyView` swaps each region for `publicRegion`, which sets `dcMods: {}`, multipliers to 1 and `encounterTable: null`, and drops `map.rules`. The result is still typed `Region`/`MapData`, with nothing to say the values are hidden rather than real. `buildDayContext(party)` feeds that view to `engine.dayPreview` for players (src/travel/context.ts:66), so a player's Travel window in, for example, a +5 Stormlands region shows Navigator DC 18 while the GM's day step rolls against 23. Days-left estimates use multiplier 1 the same way.
actionable.reason: The type can't tell 'hidden' from 'none', so consumers compute wrong numbers without knowing. That conflicts with ADR-0008's 'published DCs' goal and confuses players at the table.
actionable.suggested_fix: Mark redacted rules in the type (e.g. `rules: TravelRules | 'hidden'`, or a `redacted: true` flag on the party view). Have the player-side preview omit DCs, or label them 'before region modifiers'. Or decide DC modifiers aren't secret and pass `dcMods` through.
actionable.rationale:
80: I could not refute this finding; it holds. It is a real bug, this diff exposes it, and it triggers in practice.

- **Where the stripping happens:** `publicRegion` (src/store/index.ts:116) sets `dcMods` to {}, both multipliers to 1 and `encounterTable` to null. `partyView` also builds from `emptyMap()`, so `map.rules` never reaches the player's copy.
- **Where the wrong DCs come from:** `travel.preview()` (src/travel/index.ts:379) calls `engine.dayPreview(buildDayContext())`. For a player, `buildDayContext` defaults to `party = true` and uses `store.partyView` (src/travel/context.ts:66).
- **How the engine uses it:** `buildChecks` reads `rulesFor(map, dcHex).dcMods` (src/engine/index.ts:161-165). With dcMods empty, a player's DCs never include the region modifier.
- **Where players see it:** the Travel window renders `DC ${ch.dc}` under "Today's checks" for every user, with no GM-only branch (src/ui/travel-app.ts:86-92).
- **What the GM rolls against:** the GM's day step uses `buildDayContext(false)`, the full map (src/travel/index.ts:202). In a +5 Stormlands hex the player sees a DC 5 lower than the one rolled. The real DC then appears on the summary card, so players see the two numbers disagree.

**Why hiding the modifier is not the design:** DESIGN §6 says the summary card shows each role's DC and that a DC "hints at its terrain or region modifier; accepted as minor". So players are meant to see true DCs, and the type gives consumers no way to tell "hidden" from "none".

**Is it on a changed line?** Mostly. The stripping inside `publicRegion` already existed at 15741e7 (`dcMods: {}`, `waterMultiplier: 1`); this diff only added `rationsMultiplier: 1`. What is new is the path that feeds the player view into the engine's DC preview: src/travel/context.ts did not exist before, and neither did the player-visible "Today's checks" table. The new diff is what makes this a visible bug.

**Severity:** the effect is display only. Rolls and resolution use GM truth, so nothing is mis-resolved. Wrong DCs on screen are still confusing at the table. I score it 80 rather than higher for those two reasons: the stripping itself predates this diff, and the wrong numbers are only displayed, never rolled.

techdebt.title: Undo restores the whole caravan snapshot, reverting fund/roster/role/plan edits made after the day
techdebt.description: undo.undo() runs `store.setCaravan(snap.caravan)`, the full CaravanState captured before the day. Anything changed since then is rolled back too: funds deposits or withdrawals, travellers added or removed, seats, drivers, roles, a stopped or newly approved trip. Deposits and withdrawals also change the character's pf1 currency (pf1Adapter.setCoins), and undo does not restore that. Example: after Day 3 a player deposits 5 gp, so the PC loses 5 gp and funds go up by 500 cp. The GM then undoes Day 3, funds return to the pre-day value, the PC's 5 gp is gone and the money disappears.
techdebt.reason: DESIGN §4.13 says only the day's own changes are snapshotted and that 'Roster, role, fund and plan edits are not undoable; the GM fixes them by hand'. Invariant 4 / Done-when 2.4 ask for 'Undo restores the last day exactly', meaning the day's changes, not later edits.
techdebt.suggested_fix: Restore only the fields the day changed (position, journeyDay, trip, and funds as a delta of wages and repair), or apply the inverse of the day's deltas. Alternatively, clear the snapshot when a roster, role, fund or plan edit happens after the day.
techdebt.rationale:
70: I could not refute the finding. The mechanism is real and sits on lines this diff added, but it only triggers if someone edits between a day step and its undo, so I score it 70, below the 80 needed for verified.

What the code does:
- In `src/ledger/index.ts`, `capture()` (called from `src/travel/index.ts:210` before each day) stores `structuredClone(store.getCaravan())`, the full caravan state.
- `undo()` at line 99 writes that whole object back with `store.setCaravan(snap.caravan)`.
- Nothing invalidates the snapshot when the roster, roles, funds or plan are edited. The only callers are `capture`, `recordTime` and `undo`; `write(null)` happens only inside `undo`. The snapshot also persists on the actor flag until the next day, so it survives across sessions.

The funds path proves the money loss. `src/caravan/index.ts:202-226` changes `c.funds` (`+=`/`-=`) and calls `pf1Adapter.setCoins(actor, next)` on the character. Undo puts `c.funds` back to the pre-day value but never touches the character's coins. A deposit made after the day therefore disappears (the PC's coins are gone and the funds go back down), and a withdrawal made after the day gets duplicated.

Roster, seat, driver, role and approved-plan edits are reverted the same way. That contradicts DESIGN §4.13 ("Roster, role, fund and plan edits are not undoable; the GM fixes them by hand") and the CHANGELOG line "Undo restores the last day step only."

Why not higher: it needs a player or the GM to edit between Next Day and Undo. Undo is usually pressed right after a bad day, which keeps the chance down. The window is still plausible, though: player edits apply at once, and the snapshot stays until the next day.

techdebt.title: Rest-day repair can push party funds negative
techdebt.description: The engine allows a repair when `ctx.funds >= REPAIR_COST` (engine line 338), using funds from before the day. runDay first pays wages (`after.funds -= paid`) and then always subtracts `out.repair.cost`. With 1000 cp in funds and 300 cp of daily wages, a Rest day leaves funds at -300 cp.
techdebt.reason: DESIGN §4.6/§4.9 say repairs and wages are paid from party funds and that a shortfall pays only what it can. Funds should never go below zero, and the Done-when for 2.5 checks the 10 gp deduction.
techdebt.suggested_fix: Have the engine subtract wages before testing the repair cost (`ctx.funds - min(funds, wages) >= REPAIR_COST`), or have runDay skip the repair or clamp funds when they are short and report it on the card or whisper it to the GM.
techdebt.rationale: 75: I could not refute it; the bug is real. The repair check at src/engine/index.ts:338 tests `ctx.funds >= REPAIR_COST` (1000 cp). `ctx.funds` is copied from the caravan before the day starts (src/travel/context.ts:85). The engine also works out `wages` on every day, rest days included (engine line 317). In runDay (src/travel/index.ts:220-237), wages come off first, capped by `Math.min(after.funds, out.wages)`. After that, `after.funds -= out.repair.cost` runs with no cap and no re-check. Both lines are new in this diff (diff lines 580-595 in the 15741e7...HEAD range). Example: funds of 1000 cp and wages of 300 cp (10 trained hirelings at 3 sp each) leave -300 cp after a Rest day. Any funds from 1000 up to 1000 + wages - 1 cp go negative. The store keeps the negative value (`finite(saved.funds, 0)`). DESIGN §4.9 says that when funds fall short, only what can be paid is paid. The withdraw path also refuses to overdraw (caravan/index.ts:222). So funds should never drop below zero, and this breaks that. I scored it 75 rather than 80 or more because it only triggers in that narrow funds range on a Rest day with a Wainwright and hired travellers, so it is real but not frequent.

techdebt.title: Vehicle with unreadable or unset HP (maxHp 0) is treated as wrecked and blocks all travel
techdebt.description: vehicleInfos returns hp 0 and maxHp 0 when the vehicle actor can't be resolved or pf1 has no HP max set. The engine's vehicleBlock then reports '`v.hp <= 0` is wrecked' and pace() halves its speed (`0 <= 0/2`). The caravan can't move. The Caravan sheet guards both checks with `info.maxHp > 0`, so the vehicle card shows no Wrecked or Broken warning while the Travel window says it can't move.
techdebt.reason: The sheet and the engine disagree, so the table gets a stuck caravan with no explanation on the card. DESIGN §4.7 says the vehicle's own pf1 HP is its condition, so an unset HP should not count as wrecked.
techdebt.suggested_fix: Apply the same `maxHp > 0` guard in vehicleBlock and pace(), or treat an unresolved vehicle actor as its own explicit block reason, e.g. 'vehicle not found'.
techdebt.rationale:
45: The finding is real and sits on lines this diff changed, but it is minor, and part of the stated impact is wrong.

What checks out:
- src/engine/index.ts:82 `if (v.hp <= 0) return ... is wrecked` and :96 `if (v.hp <= v.maxHp / 2)` are new lines in the diff.
- src/travel/context.ts:43 sets hp and maxHp to 0 when the actor can't be resolved. src/pf1/index.ts:181 sets them to 0 when pf1 has no hp value or max.
- The vehicle card (src/ui/caravan-app.ts:375-376) checks `info.maxHp > 0` before showing Broken or Wrecked. The engine does no such check. So with HP 0/0 the card shows only "HP 0/0" with no Wrecked tag, while the engine blocks travel.

How it triggers: a GM drops a new pf1 vehicle actor whose HP was never filled in. pf1 vehicles plausibly start at 0/0, but I didn't check that against pf1 source. A linked vehicle actor that was later deleted does the same, since nothing prunes the link.

What's overstated:
1. The claim that the table gets "no explanation" is false. The same Caravan sheet's Speed tile (caravan-app.ts:246) shows "Stopped" with the reason "<Wagon> is wrecked". The Travel window (travel-app.ts:98) and a notification (travel/index.ts:205) show it too. Only the card's tag is missing.
2. Calling a 0-HP vehicle wrecked is a fair reading of DESIGN §4.7: the vehicle's own pf1 HP is its condition, and that HP is 0. The fix is either to make the card match the engine or to add a maxHp > 0 check in the engine. Either way the GM sees why it's stuck and fixes it by setting the wagon's HP.

Verdict: a real disagreement between the card and the engine that can happen in a fresh setup, but cosmetic, and the reason is shown elsewhere. It's "real but minor", not a hidden stuck caravan.

techdebt.title: Broken threshold uses <= half HP; DESIGN says more than half HP lost
techdebt.description: `if (v.hp <= v.maxHp / 2) miles = miles / 2;` counts a vehicle with exactly half its HP as broken. DESIGN §4.7 says 'Broken (more than half HP lost, UCombat) halves the vehicle's pace'. A 20-HP wagon at 10 HP should not be broken. The Caravan sheet (caravan-app vehicleCard) repeats the same `<=`.
techdebt.reason: An off-by-one against the published rule cited in DESIGN, on a line this diff adds.
techdebt.suggested_fix: Use `v.hp < v.maxHp / 2`, or read pf1's broken state if the vehicle exposes one. Mirror the change in the sheet.
techdebt.rationale:
70: I tried to refute this and couldn't. The off-by-one is real, but it only happens at one exact HP value.

**The code.** `src/engine/index.ts:96` is `if (v.hp <= v.maxHp / 2) miles = miles / 2;`. It is a `+` line in the diff (diff line 264), so it is new in this change. `src/ui/caravan-app.ts:375` repeats the same test for the sheet's "Broken: half pace." warning: `const broken = info.maxHp > 0 && info.hp <= info.maxHp / 2;`.

**The rule.** DESIGN.md:210 says "Broken (more than half HP lost, UCombat) halves the vehicle's pace". DESIGN.md:326 says "broken above half HP lost". The underlying PF1 rule says the same thing: an item or vehicle is broken when its damage is in excess of half its HP. At exactly half HP, exactly half has been lost, which is not more than half, so the vehicle should not be broken.

**Why the code gets it wrong.** `<=` marks the vehicle broken at exactly `maxHp/2`. A 30-HP wagon (the test fixture's default) at 15 HP, or a 20-HP cart at 10, has its pace halved when it shouldn't. The fix is `<`, in both places.

**Does it happen in play?** Yes. HP values are integers, maxHp is often even (30 and 20 in the fixtures), and daily d4–d10 wear can land exactly on half. When it does, the caravan's pace for the day is halved, which is a visible gameplay error. The existing test, "broken halves the vehicle's pace" (`test/engine/engine.test.ts:132`), never tests the exact-half case, so nothing catches this.

**Score.** It is real and on new lines, but it only triggers at that single HP value, so I scored it 70 rather than 75+.

techdebt.title: 0.1.x map migration only happens in memory; the scene flag keeps the dropped fields
techdebt.description: getMap() calls migrateMap() on every read when `version !== MAP_VERSION` but never writes the result back. A 0.1.x scene keeps difficulty, encounterMod, custom tags, stormThreshold and route days/effects/prompts in its flag until the GM happens to save through the painter. The migration also reruns on every getMap call, i.e. every render and preview.
techdebt.reason: The ROADMAP 2.1 Done-when requires 'a 0.1.x scene loads with its terrain mapped per §4.2 and no dropped field left in its data'.
techdebt.suggested_fix: On ready (or the first getMap on the GM client), persist the migrated map with store.setMap for scenes whose flag version is older, and whisper the GM to review it per DESIGN §4.2.
techdebt.rationale:
35: The mechanics are real, and line 184 is new in this diff. getMap() runs migrateMap() whenever the saved version is not 2 and never writes the result back, so the raw scene flag keeps the 0.1.x fields until the GM's next setMap. setMap rewrites the whole JSON string, so any painter edit removes them.

The invariant break is weak, though. Nothing in the code reads the flag except through getMap: layer, tooltip, painter, travel context, caravan-app, travel-app and partyView all go through it, and migrateMap whitelists fields. So no dropped field ever reaches behaviour or a player view.

DESIGN §4.2 says "Existing maps migrate on load ... The GM reviews the result". That describes migrating on read, with the GM persisting the result. The Done-when line "a 0.1.x scene loads with ... no dropped field left in its data" was put into practice by test/canvas/migrate.test.ts ("leaves no dropped field anywhere"), which checks the loaded result. That reads "its data" as the loaded map, not the stored flag.

Writing back on load would also need a GM-only hook, because setMap requires the GM. Re-running the migration on every getMap call only costs time, O(hexes), and only for scenes not yet re-saved. It is a small inefficiency, not a correctness bug.

Net: real but minor. It is arguably the intended design, it has no visible effect, and it fixes itself on the first GM save. It is not a verified invariant break.

techdebt.title: Approve does not re-check the course against the caravan's current position
techdebt.description: setPlanHandler checks validCourse(position, course) only when the plan is submitted. The GM can then move the caravan (caravan.place is allowed while no trip is active) and approve the old plan. approve() copies plan.course into the trip unchecked. The engine's moveToday never checks that course[0] is adjacent to position, so the caravan jumps along a course that doesn't start next to it.
techdebt.reason: DESIGN §4.10 says a course is a chain of adjacent hexes from the caravan and needs GM approval. The approval should not accept a stale course.
techdebt.suggested_fix: In approve(), call validCourse(before.position, plan.course) and refuse or clear the course when it fails. Or clear plan.course in caravan.place when the position changes.
techdebt.rationale:
75: I tried to refute this and couldn't. The finding holds, and it is on lines this diff added: `travel.approve()` is new, and `after.trip = { ... course: [...plan.course] ... }` is at diff line 822 (around src/travel/index.ts:322).

How it triggers:
(1) A player calls `setPlan`. `setPlanHandler` checks `validCourse(before.position, req.course)` against position A and stores `plan.course`.
(2) The GM moves the caravan using "place caravan" in src/ui/caravan-app.ts:677, which calls `caravanService.place` in src/caravan/index.ts:319. `place` only refuses when `c.trip` is set. It overwrites `c.position` and `c.sceneId`, and never clears or re-checks `c.plan`. It can even move the caravan to a different scene.
(3) The GM clicks Approve. In src/ui/travel-app.ts:144-146, `ready` checks only that the course is non-empty and that there is a position. It does no adjacency check. `approve()` copies `plan.course` without checking it.
(4) `runDay` calls `engine.moveToday` (src/engine/index.ts:127). That function reads `course[0]` and `course[i]` and checks only `passable` and `roadKind`. It never checks that `course[0]` is adjacent to `position`. So `out.end` becomes a non-adjacent hex, and the code writes it to `position` and moves the token there.

No other guard catches this: `buildDayContext` passes `trip.course` straight through, and nothing else re-runs `validCourse`.

Why 75 and not higher: it only happens when the GM moves the caravan after a plan is submitted and before approving it. That is plausible, for example fixing a mis-placed token, but it is not the common flow. The GM also has to approve without noticing the course drawn on the map. The effect is real (the caravan jumps, and on a scene change it follows hex keys from the other scene), but undo can recover it.

techdebt.title: Players' seat/drive/pull edits are applied without whispering the GM
techdebt.description: addActor, removeActor and funds whisper the GM when a player acts. setSeat, setDriver and setTeam (lines 143, 154, 173) apply silently.
techdebt.reason: DESIGN §4.13: players 'edit the roster with actors and vehicles they own — add, remove, seat, drive, pull (applied at once; the GM is whispered, since it changes daily use)'.
techdebt.suggested_fix: Add the same `if (!user?.isGM) await whisperGM(...)` call to setSeat, setDriver and setTeam.
techdebt.rationale: 65: I could not refute the finding. In src/caravan/index.ts, which this diff adds in full, addActor (line 122), removeActor (line 139) and funds (lines 228-231) each call whisperGM when the user is not a GM. setSeat (143-152), setDriver (154-171) and setTeam (173-185) just return save(c) and send nothing. Nothing else sends the message either: grepping for whisper and ChatMessage turns up whispers only in caravan/index.ts and travel/index.ts. DESIGN.md §4.13, also changed in this diff, says roster edits by players, explicitly 'add, remove, seat, drive, pull', are 'applied at once; the GM is whispered, since it changes daily use'. No ADR in DECISIONS.md exempts seat, drive or pull, so the code does not match the spec. This happens every time a player seats, drives or pulls through caravan.setSeat, setDriver or setTeam from the sheet or an agent: the active GM's client applies the change with no whisper. The existing tests cover the whisper only for add and funds. I scored it below 75 because it does not break any of the four load-bearing invariants in DESIGN §5 or CLAUDE.md. Invariant 2 (the GM is the only writer) still holds, because these requests go through the authority, which checks ownership. The fault is a missing GM notification against a §4.13 spec line, not a violation of an invariant, so it is real and frequent but moderate in impact.

techdebt.title: Hireling wages always default to 0 instead of the CRB rates
techdebt.description: travellerFor sets `wage: 0` for every actor, NPC hirelings included. pf1Adapter.playerOwners is available and could tell PCs from hirelings, but it isn't used.
techdebt.reason: DESIGN §4.9: 'each traveller has a daily wage, default none for PCs; hirelings default to the CRB rates (trained 3 sp, untrained 1 sp)'. The default is part of the Caravan sheet's wages feature (ROADMAP 2.2).
techdebt.suggested_fix: In travellerFor, default wage to 10 cp (untrained) or 30 cp (trained) when the actor has no player owner, and keep the GM override in updateTraveller.
techdebt.rationale: 72: I could not refute it. The finding is real, it sits on a line this diff changed, and it triggers whenever an NPC is added. In the diff, `rosterMemberFor` became `travellerFor`, and the line `return { actorUuid, name, food, water, wage: 0, seat: null }` at src/pf1/index.ts:144 is new. The old code did compute `npc: pf1Adapter.playerOwners(actor).length === 0`. The new code drops that check, and nothing else in the file uses `playerOwners` to set a wage. The only way into the caravan for a non-vehicle actor is `addActor` (src/caravan/index.ts:120 calls `c.travellers.push(pf1Adapter.travellerFor(actor))`), so every hireling the GM adds starts at 0 cp. The engine (src/engine/index.ts:317) and the daily payout (src/travel/index.ts:220, `if (out.wages > 0)`) then pay nothing and say nothing. That contradicts DESIGN §4.9 ("hirelings default to the CRB rates (trained 3 sp, untrained 1 sp)"). It also contradicts the 0.2.5 CHANGELOG, which says "NPC wages (CRB: 3 sp trained, 1 sp untrained) are paid from it every day". The 0.1.x migration in src/store/index.ts:51 also writes `wage: 0`, so migrated NPCs get no default either. No test checks a non-zero default, and test/integration/caravan.test.ts:78 expects a horse to have `wage: 0`. Two points keep this below 75. First, the GM can type a wage per traveller on the Caravan sheet (`updateTraveller` / the wage input in caravan-app.ts), so this is a missing default, not lost data or a crash. Second, the suggested fix is not as simple as calling `playerOwners`: unowned animals such as a horse or draft team are also NPCs and should stay at 0, and nothing in the actor marks a hireling as trained or untrained. Verdict: a confirmed, moderate gap against the spec and the changelog, likely to show up in real play, but it has a manual workaround.

techdebt.title: Course-plotting clicks are not swallowed: PIXI/Foundry (and the open Hex Painter) still get the pointerdown
techdebt.description: onPointerDown is added on canvas.app.view with capture:true at canvasReady and calls event.stopPropagation(). techdebt.title: Engine and Caravan sheet disagree on 'wrecked' for vehicles with maxHp 0

The broken/wrecked predicates live in two modules with different definitions.
techdebt.reason: A derived state is defined twice and the definitions don't match, so the sheet tells the GM the vehicle is fine while Next Day refuses to move.
techdebt.suggested_fix: Export one `vehicleCondition(info): 'ok' | 'broken' | 'wrecked'` (pure, from the engine) and use it in both places. Decide once how maxHp 0 is treated, e.g. as unconfigured: no HP rules, plus a separate 'HP not set' warning.
techdebt.rationale: 50: The mismatch is real, and it sits on lines this diff added. src/engine/index.ts:82 `if (v.hp <= 0) return \`${v.name} is wrecked\`` is new in the diff. It has no maxHp guard. The card in src/ui/caravan-app.ts:375-376 does guard with `info.maxHp > 0 &&`. all.title: Undo restores the whole caravan snapshot, reverting fund/roster/role/plan edits made after the day
all.description: undo.undo() runs `store.setCaravan(snap.caravan)`, the full CaravanState captured before the day. Anything changed since then is rolled back too: funds deposits or withdrawals, travellers added or removed, seats, drivers, roles, a stopped or newly approved trip. Deposits and withdrawals also change the character's pf1 currency (pf1Adapter.setCoins), and undo does not restore that. Example: after Day 3 a player deposits 5 gp, so the PC loses 5 gp and funds go up by 500 cp. The GM then undoes Day 3, funds return to the pre-day value, the PC's 5 gp is gone and the money disappears.
all.reason: DESIGN §4.13 says only the day's own changes are snapshotted and that 'Roster, role, fund and plan edits are not undoable; the GM fixes them by hand'. Invariant 4 / Done-when 2.4 ask for 'Undo restores the last day exactly', meaning the day's changes, not later edits.
all.suggested_fix: Restore only the fields the day changed (position, journeyDay, trip, and funds as a delta of wages and repair), or apply the inverse of the day's deltas. Alternatively, clear the snapshot when a roster, role, fund or plan edit happens after the day.
all.rationale:
70: I could not refute the finding. The mechanism is real and sits on lines this diff added, but it only triggers if someone edits between a day step and its undo, so I score it 70, below the 80 needed for verified.

What the code does:
- In `src/ledger/index.ts`, `capture()` (called from `src/travel/index.ts:210` before each day) stores `structuredClone(store.getCaravan())`, the full caravan state.
- `undo()` at line 99 writes that whole object back with `store.setCaravan(snap.caravan)`.
- Nothing invalidates the snapshot when the roster, roles, funds or plan are edited. The only callers are `capture`, `recordTime` and `undo`; `write(null)` happens only inside `undo`. The snapshot also persists on the actor flag until the next day, so it survives across sessions.

The funds path proves the money loss. `src/caravan/index.ts:202-226` changes `c.funds` (`+=`/`-=`) and calls `pf1Adapter.setCoins(actor, next)` on the character. Undo puts `c.funds` back to the pre-day value but never touches the character's coins. A deposit made after the day therefore disappears (the PC's coins are gone and the funds go back down), and a withdrawal made after the day gets duplicated.

Roster, seat, driver, role and approved-plan edits are reverted the same way. That contradicts DESIGN §4.13 ("Roster, role, fund and plan edits are not undoable; the GM fixes them by hand") and the CHANGELOG line "Undo restores the last day step only."

Why not higher: it needs a player or the GM to edit between Next Day and Undo. Undo is usually pressed right after a bad day, which keeps the chance down. The window is still plausible, though: player edits apply at once, and the snapshot stays until the next day.

all.title: Rest-day repair can push party funds negative
all.description: The engine allows a repair when `ctx.funds >= REPAIR_COST` (engine line 338), using funds from before the day. runDay first pays wages (`after.funds -= paid`) and then always subtracts `out.repair.cost`. With 1000 cp in funds and 300 cp of daily wages, a Rest day leaves funds at -300 cp.
all.reason: DESIGN §4.6/§4.9 say repairs and wages are paid from party funds and that a shortfall pays only what it can. Funds should never go below zero, and the Done-when for 2.5 checks the 10 gp deduction.
all.suggested_fix: Have the engine subtract wages before testing the repair cost (`ctx.funds - min(funds, wages) >= REPAIR_COST`), or have runDay skip the repair or clamp funds when they are short and report it on the card or whisper it to the GM.
all.rationale: 75: I could not refute it; the bug is real. The repair check at src/engine/index.ts:338 tests `ctx.funds >= REPAIR_COST` (1000 cp). `ctx.funds` is copied from the caravan before the day starts (src/travel/context.ts:85). The engine also works out `wages` on every day, rest days included (engine line 317). In runDay (src/travel/index.ts:220-237), wages come off first, capped by `Math.min(after.funds, out.wages)`. After that, `after.funds -= out.repair.cost` runs with no cap and no re-check. Both lines are new in this diff (diff lines 580-595 in the 15741e7...HEAD range). Example: funds of 1000 cp and wages of 300 cp (10 trained hirelings at 3 sp each) leave -300 cp after a Rest day. Any funds from 1000 up to 1000 + wages - 1 cp go negative. The store keeps the negative value (`finite(saved.funds, 0)`). DESIGN §4.9 says that when funds fall short, only what can be paid is paid. The withdraw path also refuses to overdraw (caravan/index.ts:222). So funds should never drop below zero, and this breaks that. I scored it 75 rather than 80 or more because it only triggers in that narrow funds range on a Rest day with a Wainwright and hired travellers, so it is real but not frequent.

all.title: Vehicle with unreadable or unset HP (maxHp 0) is treated as wrecked and blocks all travel
all.description: vehicleInfos returns hp 0 and maxHp 0 when the vehicle actor can't be resolved or pf1 has no HP max set. The engine's vehicleBlock then reports '`v.hp <= 0` is wrecked' and pace() halves its speed (`0 <= 0/2`). The caravan can't move. The Caravan sheet guards both checks with `info.maxHp > 0`, so the vehicle card shows no Wrecked or Broken warning while the Travel window says it can't move.
all.reason: The sheet and the engine disagree, so the table gets a stuck caravan with no explanation on the card. DESIGN §4.7 says the vehicle's own pf1 HP is its condition, so an unset HP should not count as wrecked.
all.suggested_fix: Apply the same `maxHp > 0` guard in vehicleBlock and pace(), or treat an unresolved vehicle actor as its own explicit block reason, e.g. 'vehicle not found'.
all.rationale:
45: The finding is real and sits on lines this diff changed, but it is minor, and part of the stated impact is wrong.

What checks out:
- src/engine/index.ts:82 `if (v.hp <= 0) return ... is wrecked` and :96 `if (v.hp <= v.maxHp / 2)` are new lines in the diff.
- src/travel/context.ts:43 sets hp and maxHp to 0 when the actor can't be resolved. src/pf1/index.ts:181 sets them to 0 when pf1 has no hp value or max.
- The vehicle card (src/ui/caravan-app.ts:375-376) checks `info.maxHp > 0` before showing Broken or Wrecked. The engine does no such check. So with HP 0/0 the card shows only "HP 0/0" with no Wrecked tag, while the engine blocks travel.

How it triggers: a GM drops a new pf1 vehicle actor whose HP was never filled in. pf1 vehicles plausibly start at 0/0, but I didn't check that against pf1 source. A linked vehicle actor that was later deleted does the same, since nothing prunes the link.

What's overstated:
1. The claim that the table gets "no explanation" is false. The same Caravan sheet's Speed tile (caravan-app.ts:246) shows "Stopped" with the reason "<Wagon> is wrecked". The Travel window (travel-app.ts:98) and a notification (travel/index.ts:205) show it too. Only the card's tag is missing.
2. Calling a 0-HP vehicle wrecked is a fair reading of DESIGN §4.7: the vehicle's own pf1 HP is its condition, and that HP is 0. The fix is either to make the card match the engine or to add a maxHp > 0 check in the engine. Either way the GM sees why it's stuck and fixes it by setting the wagon's HP.

Verdict: a real disagreement between the card and the engine that can happen in a fresh setup, but cosmetic, and the reason is shown elsewhere. It's "real but minor", not a hidden stuck caravan.

all.title: Broken threshold uses <= half HP; DESIGN says more than half HP lost
all.description: `if (v.hp <= v.maxHp / 2) miles = miles / 2;` counts a vehicle with exactly half its HP as broken. DESIGN §4.7 says 'Broken (more than half HP lost, UCombat) halves the vehicle's pace'. A 20-HP wagon at 10 HP should not be broken. The Caravan sheet (caravan-app vehicleCard) repeats the same `<=`.
all.reason: An off-by-one against the published rule cited in DESIGN, on a line this diff adds.
all.suggested_fix: Use `v.hp < v.maxHp / 2`, or read pf1's broken state if the vehicle exposes one. Mirror the change in the sheet.
all.rationale:
70: I tried to refute this and couldn't. The off-by-one is real, but it only happens at one exact HP value.

**The code.** `src/engine/index.ts:96` is `if (v.hp <= v.maxHp / 2) miles = miles / 2;`. It is a `+` line in the diff (diff line 264), so it is new in this change. `src/ui/caravan-app.ts:375` repeats the same test for the sheet's "Broken: half pace." warning: `const broken = info.maxHp > 0 && info.hp <= info.maxHp / 2;`.

**The rule.** DESIGN.md:210 says "Broken (more than half HP lost, UCombat) halves the vehicle's pace". DESIGN.md:326 says "broken above half HP lost". The underlying PF1 rule says the same thing: an item or vehicle is broken when its damage is in excess of half its HP. At exactly half HP, exactly half has been lost, which is not more than half, so the vehicle should not be broken.

**Why the code gets it wrong.** `<=` marks the vehicle broken at exactly `maxHp/2`. A 30-HP wagon (the test fixture's default) at 15 HP, or a 20-HP cart at 10, has its pace halved when it shouldn't. The fix is `<`, in both places.

**Does it happen in play?** Yes. HP values are integers, maxHp is often even (30 and 20 in the fixtures), and daily d4–d10 wear can land exactly on half. When it does, the caravan's pace for the day is halved, which is a visible gameplay error. The existing test, "broken halves the vehicle's pace" (`test/engine/engine.test.ts:132`), never tests the exact-half case, so nothing catches this.

**Score.** It is real and on new lines, but it only triggers at that single HP value, so I scored it 70 rather than 75+.

all.title: 0.1.x map migration only happens in memory; the scene flag keeps the dropped fields
all.description: getMap() calls migrateMap() on every read when `version !== MAP_VERSION` but never writes the result back. A 0.1.x scene keeps difficulty, encounterMod, custom tags, stormThreshold and route days/effects/prompts in its flag until the GM happens to save through the painter. The migration also reruns on every getMap call, i.e. every render and preview.
all.reason: The ROADMAP 2.1 Done-when requires 'a 0.1.x scene loads with its terrain mapped per §4.2 and no dropped field left in its data'.
all.suggested_fix: On ready (or the first getMap on the GM client), persist the migrated map with store.setMap for scenes whose flag version is older, and whisper the GM to review it per DESIGN §4.2.
all.rationale:
35: The mechanics are real, and line 184 is new in this diff. getMap() runs migrateMap() whenever the saved version is not 2 and never writes the result back, so the raw scene flag keeps the 0.1.x fields until the GM's next setMap. setMap rewrites the whole JSON string, so any painter edit removes them.

The invariant break is weak, though. Nothing in the code reads the flag except through getMap: layer, tooltip, painter, travel context, caravan-app, travel-app and partyView all go through it, and migrateMap whitelists fields. So no dropped field ever reaches behaviour or a player view.

DESIGN §4.2 says "Existing maps migrate on load ... The GM reviews the result". That describes migrating on read, with the GM persisting the result. The Done-when line "a 0.1.x scene loads with ... no dropped field left in its data" was put into practice by test/canvas/migrate.test.ts ("leaves no dropped field anywhere"), which checks the loaded result. That reads "its data" as the loaded map, not the stored flag.

Writing back on load would also need a GM-only hook, because setMap requires the GM. Re-running the migration on every getMap call only costs time, O(hexes), and only for scenes not yet re-saved. It is a small inefficiency, not a correctness bug.

Net: real but minor. It is arguably the intended design, it has no visible effect, and it fixes itself on the first GM save. It is not a verified invariant break.

all.title: Approve does not re-check the course against the caravan's current position
all.description: setPlanHandler checks validCourse(position, course) only when the plan is submitted. The GM can then move the caravan (caravan.place is allowed while no trip is active) and approve the old plan. approve() copies plan.course into the trip unchecked. The engine's moveToday never checks that course[0] is adjacent to position, so the caravan jumps along a course that doesn't start next to it.
all.reason: DESIGN §4.10 says a course is a chain of adjacent hexes from the caravan and needs GM approval. The approval should not accept a stale course.
all.suggested_fix: In approve(), call validCourse(before.position, plan.course) and refuse or clear the course when it fails. Or clear plan.course in caravan.place when the position changes.
all.rationale:
75: I tried to refute this and couldn't. The finding holds, and it is on lines this diff added: `travel.approve()` is new, and `after.trip = { ... course: [...plan.course] ... }` is at diff line 822 (around src/travel/index.ts:322).

How it triggers:
(1) A player calls `setPlan`. `setPlanHandler` checks `validCourse(before.position, req.course)` against position A and stores `plan.course`.
(2) The GM moves the caravan using "place caravan" in src/ui/caravan-app.ts:677, which calls `caravanService.place` in src/caravan/index.ts:319. `place` only refuses when `c.trip` is set. It overwrites `c.position` and `c.sceneId`, and never clears or re-checks `c.plan`. It can even move the caravan to a different scene.
(3) The GM clicks Approve. In src/ui/travel-app.ts:144-146, `ready` checks only that the course is non-empty and that there is a position. It does no adjacency check. `approve()` copies `plan.course` without checking it.
(4) `runDay` calls `engine.moveToday` (src/engine/index.ts:127). That function reads `course[0]` and `course[i]` and checks only `passable` and `roadKind`. It never checks that `course[0]` is adjacent to `position`. So `out.end` becomes a non-adjacent hex, and the code writes it to `position` and moves the token there.

No other guard catches this: `buildDayContext` passes `trip.course` straight through, and nothing else re-runs `validCourse`.

Why 75 and not higher: it only happens when the GM moves the caravan after a plan is submitted and before approving it. That is plausible, for example fixing a mis-placed token, but it is not the common flow. The GM also has to approve without noticing the course drawn on the map. The effect is real (the caravan jumps, and on a scene change it follows hex keys from the other scene), but undo can recover it.

all.title: New adapter methods write pf1 system data paths directly (vehicle HP, currency)
all.description: setVehicleHp does `actor.update({"system.attributes.hp.value": ...})` and setCoins does `actor.update({"system.currency.<k>": ...})` (line 193). Both are new in this diff and write pf1 system data directly instead of going through a pf1 public API.
all.reason: CLAUDE.md Tech conventions: 'pf1 access only through its public API (actor rolls, conditions); never write pf1 system data paths directly.'
all.suggested_fix: Use pf1's public API where one exists (e.g. actor.applyDamage for wear, or the currency helpers if pf1 provides them). Where none exists, record the exception in an ADR or TECH-DEBT row so the convention is consciously waived, not silently broken.
all.rationale: 20: The lines are real and new in this diff. src/pf1/index.ts:184-185 does `actor.update({"system.attributes.hp.value": Math.round(hp)})`, and lines 193-196 build `system.currency.{pp,gp,sp,cp}` updates, with values floored and clamped at 0. Through the correctness lens, though, this produces no wrong result. Vehicle HP and coins live at these documented pf1 data paths, the writes are clamped and rounded, and `actor.update` is Foundry's public document API. pf1 has no dedicated public setter for currency or vehicle HP, so the CLAUDE.md rule cannot be met any other way. DESIGN.md section 3 (line 60) assigns 'vehicle HP and inventory, coin' to the src/pf1/ adapter. Section 4.13 (line 273) says the day step changes vehicle HP and party funds. So the design calls for these writes, and they sit inside the adapter, the layer that is allowed to touch pf1. Code from before this diff already writes pf1 system paths the same way: `"system.quantity"` via `item.update` and `updateContainerContents` in src/store/index.ts and src/ledger/index.ts at 15741e7. The project has therefore always read 'public API' to include document.update. At most this is a wording mismatch with the CLAUDE.md convention (a docs nitpick), not a bug that triggers in practice. One HP risk I could not check (pf1 versions that store character HP as an offset) is a different issue from this finding, and it may not apply to vehicle actors.

all.title: Players' seat/drive/pull edits are applied without whispering the GM
all.description: addActor, removeActor and funds whisper the GM when a player acts. setSeat, setDriver and setTeam (lines 143, 154, 173) apply silently.
all.reason: DESIGN §4.13: players 'edit the roster with actors and vehicles they own — add, remove, seat, drive, pull (applied at once; the GM is whispered, since it changes daily use)'.
all.suggested_fix: Add the same `if (!user?.isGM) await whisperGM(...)` call to setSeat, setDriver and setTeam.
all.rationale: 65: I could not refute the finding. In src/caravan/index.ts, which this diff adds in full, addActor (line 122), removeActor (line 139) and funds (lines 228-231) each call whisperGM when the user is not a GM. setSeat (143-152), setDriver (154-171) and setTeam (173-185) just return save(c) and send nothing. Nothing else sends the message either: grepping for whisper and ChatMessage turns up whispers only in caravan/index.ts and travel/index.ts. DESIGN.md §4.13, also changed in this diff, says roster edits by players, explicitly 'add, remove, seat, drive, pull', are 'applied at once; the GM is whispered, since it changes daily use'. No ADR in DECISIONS.md exempts seat, drive or pull, so the code does not match the spec. This happens every time a player seats, drives or pulls through caravan.setSeat, setDriver or setTeam from the sheet or an agent: the active GM's client applies the change with no whisper. The existing tests cover the whisper only for add and funds. I scored it below 75 because it does not break any of the four load-bearing invariants in DESIGN §5 or CLAUDE.md. Invariant 2 (the GM is the only writer) still holds, because these requests go through the authority, which checks ownership. The fault is a missing GM notification against a §4.13 spec line, not a violation of an invariant, so it is real and frequent but moderate in impact.

all.title: Hireling wages always default to 0 instead of the CRB rates
all.description: travellerFor sets `wage: 0` for every actor, NPC hirelings included. pf1Adapter.playerOwners is available and could tell PCs from hirelings, but it isn't used.
all.reason: DESIGN §4.9: 'each traveller has a daily wage, default none for PCs; hirelings default to the CRB rates (trained 3 sp, untrained 1 sp)'. The default is part of the Caravan sheet's wages feature (ROADMAP 2.2).
all.suggested_fix: In travellerFor, default wage to 10 cp (untrained) or 30 cp (trained) when the actor has no player owner, and keep the GM override in updateTraveller.
all.rationale: 72: I could not refute it. The finding is real, it sits on a line this diff changed, and it triggers whenever an NPC is added. In the diff, `rosterMemberFor` became `travellerFor`, and the line `return { actorUuid, name, food, water, wage: 0, seat: null }` at src/pf1/index.ts:144 is new. The old code did compute `npc: pf1Adapter.playerOwners(actor).length === 0`. The new code drops that check, and nothing else in the file uses `playerOwners` to set a wage. The only way into the caravan for a non-vehicle actor is `addActor` (src/caravan/index.ts:120 calls `c.travellers.push(pf1Adapter.travellerFor(actor))`), so every hireling the GM adds starts at 0 cp. The engine (src/engine/index.ts:317) and the daily payout (src/travel/index.ts:220, `if (out.wages > 0)`) then pay nothing and say nothing. That contradicts DESIGN §4.9 ("hirelings default to the CRB rates (trained 3 sp, untrained 1 sp)"). It also contradicts the 0.2.5 CHANGELOG, which says "NPC wages (CRB: 3 sp trained, 1 sp untrained) are paid from it every day". The 0.1.x migration in src/store/index.ts:51 also writes `wage: 0`, so migrated NPCs get no default either. No test checks a non-zero default, and test/integration/caravan.test.ts:78 expects a horse to have `wage: 0`. Two points keep this below 75. First, the GM can type a wage per traveller on the Caravan sheet (`updateTraveller` / the wage input in caravan-app.ts), so this is a missing default, not lost data or a crash. Second, the suggested fix is not as simple as calling `playerOwners`: unowned animals such as a horse or draft team are also NPCs and should stay at 0, and nothing in the actor marks a hireling as trained or untrained. Verdict: a confirmed, moderate gap against the spec and the changelog, likely to show up in real play, but it has a manual workaround.

all.title: Large rider body weight is 1400 lb; DESIGN specifies 8 x Medium (1440 lb)
all.description: BODY_WEIGHT has `lg: 1400` and `huge: 11000`. DESIGN §4.7 sets 'Medium 180 lb, Large x8 of Medium', which gives 1440 lb for Large and about 11520 lb for Huge at the same x8 step. These provisional numbers are hardcoded literals that don't match the documented defaults the owner is asked to confirm (§4.14).
all.reason: The hardcoded value doesn't match the provisional default DESIGN documents, so the owner would be confirming one number while the code uses another.
all.suggested_fix: Derive the table from Medium x 8 per size step, or update DESIGN §4.7 to the chosen numbers. Consider making the table a tunable, since §4.14 lists it as awaiting the owner's confirmation.
all.rationale:
25: The finding points at real, newly added lines. In src/pf1/index.ts, BODY_WEIGHT now has lg: 1400 and huge: 11000. DESIGN.md:198-199 says "Small 40 lb, Medium 180 lb, Large x8 of Medium... (provisional)", and 8 x 180 = 1440. So the code and the doc differ, but treating that as a correctness bug is weak:
(1) The whole table is a rounded x8-per-step chain: 1400*8 is about 11200 -> 11000, 11000*8 = 88000 -> 90000, 90000*8 = 720000 -> 700000. DESIGN's "x8 of Medium..." with its ellipsis and "provisional" tag describes a rough rule of thumb, and the code follows it with rounded numbers.
(2) The doc itself doesn't apply x8 strictly: Small at 40 lb is not 180/8, so the x8 wording is not a precise spec the code could be wrong against.
(3) The practical effect is tiny. The value only matters for a Large rider beyond a vehicle's seats, counted as cargo, where it is 40 lb lighter (about 2.8%), and the default is provisional and up for the owner to confirm (DESIGN.md:277).
At most this is a documentation-precision nit: either list the exact numbers in DESIGN or use 1440 in the code. It is not a math error that produces a meaningfully wrong result.

all.title: Travel all can burn up to 60 days when the Navigator is vacant or keeps getting lost
all.description: travelAll loops up to 60 runDay() calls. It stops only on null, end of trip, a non-'nothing' encounter, or pace.blocked. A vacant Navigator fails automatically off-road (engine resolveDay: actorUuid null -> success false), so lost=true, moved=[], and the trip never ends. If the hex has no encounter table, or the table returns nothing, every one of the 60 iterations drains rations and water, pays wages, rolls wear on nothing, and advances world time by a day. Undo only restores the last day (ledger keeps one snapshot). Roles do not carry over from 0.1.x data (migrateCaravan only keeps saved.roles, which 0.1.x caravans did not have), so on a migrated world tonight every role starts vacant. The first Travel all on a road-less course would then spend 60 days of supplies and time, and Undo cannot fix it.
all.reason: In live play this destroys supplies and world time with no recovery path. The migration path makes it likely on first use.
all.suggested_fix: In travelAll, break when out.lost (or when no hex was moved), and/or refuse to run Travel all while the Navigator role is vacant. Alternatively, cap Travel all at the course's estimated days.
all.rationale:
80: I could not refute this finding. Every link in the chain checks out in the code, and the loop is new in this diff (travelAll was added in 912eaa4).

1. **The loop never sees the stall.** travelAll (src/travel/index.ts:342-353) runs up to 60 runDay() calls. It breaks only on four conditions: a null result, the trip ending, `lastEncounter`, or `out.pace.blocked`. Nothing checks `out.lost` or an empty `out.moved`.

2. **A vacant Navigator always fails off-road.** In src/engine/index.ts, resolveDay sets `success: false` when `actorUuid === null`. Only road hexes skip the check, because `auto` is set from `road`. That makes `lost = pv.moving && !ok("navigator")` true and `moved` empty. In the travel case, `lost` sets `done = false`, so the trip never ends. `pace.blocked` stays null because the caravan can still move; it just got lost.

3. **Each lost day still costs a full day.** runDay drains rations and water, pays wages, applies vehicle wear, increments journeyDay, advances world time by a day, and posts a chat card, all without making progress.

4. **The encounter break rarely fires.** DEFAULT_RULES has `encounterTable: null`, and `lastEncounter = !!table && !isNothing(text)`. A hex with no table can never stop the loop, and a table that returns nothing doesn't either.

5. **Undo restores only one day.** The comment in src/ledger/index.ts says each day's snapshot replaces the previous one, so only the last day can be undone.

6. **Migrated caravans start with every role vacant.** migrateCaravan (src/store/index.ts) keeps only `saved.roles` holders. The 0.1.x types have no per-caravan role holders, so `roles` comes out as `{}`. A fresh caravan with no Navigator assigned hits the same path.

There is one mitigation, which is why the score isn't higher. The trigger needs an off-road course, a vacant Navigator (or one who keeps failing), and the GM pressing Travel all. The per-day chat cards would announce "lost the way" each day, but the loop runs without stopping, so the GM can't step in. This is a real correctness bug that is likely in tonight's session.

all.title: Course-plotting clicks are not swallowed: PIXI/Foundry (and the open Hex Painter) still get the pointerdown
all.description: onPointerDown is added on canvas.app.view with capture:true at canvasReady and calls event.stopPropagation(). PIXI 7.4.3, which Foundry v13 bundles, already registers its own pointerdown listener on that same element with capture=true (dist/pixi.js:14440: domElement.addEventListener('pointerdown', this.onPointerDown, !0)), and it registered first. Both listeners sit on the event target, so stopPropagation does not stop PIXI's listener, and PIXI's runs first anyway. Each plotting click therefore also reaches Foundry's canvas interaction: token select/deselect, starting a drag-select, or grabbing the caravan token. It also reaches canvas.stage 'pointerdown' listeners such as the Hex Painter (painter.ts:173). If the GM plots a course with the painter open, each destination or waypoint click also paints, erases, or toggles tags on that hex with the active brush and saves it to the map.
all.reason: The code means to take over the click, but the click leaks through. With the painter open it silently corrupts map data, and for every user it causes stray token interactions.
all.suggested_fix: Swallow the event before PIXI sees it: listen on an ancestor in capture phase (e.g. document or canvas.app.view.parentElement with capture:true) and call stopImmediatePropagation()+preventDefault(). Or temporarily disable canvas.app.renderer.events features.click while plotting. Also close or ignore the painter brush while plotting.
all.rationale:
55: I could not refute the mechanism, but the impact is smaller than the finding says, and the "invariant" lens does not apply.

What holds up:
- src/canvas/course.ts is new in this diff. Line 111 adds onPointerDown to canvas.app.view with { capture: true } at canvasReady. Line 64 calls only event.stopPropagation() and preventDefault(), never stopImmediatePropagation().
- I fetched pixi.js@7.4.3 from unpkg (Foundry v13 bundles PIXI 7.4.x; I did not check that exact version in a local Foundry install). Line 14440 shows `this.domElement.addEventListener("pointerdown", this.onPointerDown, !0)`. PIXI adds this listener when the renderer is created, well before canvasReady.
- Both listeners are capture listeners on the target element, so they run in the order they were added. PIXI's runs first.
- PIXI's onPointerDown (line 14356) never checks defaultPrevented or propagation. It maps the event onto the federated stage tree either way.
- So canvas.stage 'pointerdown' listeners still fire. That includes the Hex Painter (painter.ts:173). Its handler (painter.ts:100) starts a stroke and calls paint(key). The stroke is saved on pointerup, so a plotting click with the painter open would apply the active brush to that hex. Foundry's own canvas interaction (token select/release) also still sees the click.

What weakens it:
- No declared invariant in CLAUDE.md is broken. The painter write is still the GM writing, and nothing hidden reaches players. Under the invariant lens it is a correctness bug, not an invariant breach.
- The map-corruption case is GM-only. It needs the painter open while plotting from the travel app, which is plausible during prep but not frequent.
- For everyone else, the leak mostly means releasing or selecting tokens on the clicked hex. That is a cosmetic nuisance, not data damage.

Verdict: real, on a changed line, and it triggers whenever course plotting is used. The common-case impact is minor and the serious case is rare, so the score lands between "real but minor" and "important".

all.title: Approve does not revalidate the plan's course against the current position; a stale course teleports the caravan
all.description: setPlanHandler validates the course against the caravan's position when the plan is set. caravan.place() (caravan/index.ts:344) later changes c.position and c.sceneId without clearing c.plan.course, and approve() copies plan.course into the trip unchecked. The engine never checks adjacency (moveToday moves straight into course[0] from ctx.position). Example: players plot a course, then the GM re-places the caravan (Place on map, or a canvas drop). The GM approves, and on Next Day the caravan jumps to a hex that may be far away, possibly on another scene's coordinates, and the token moves there.
all.reason: This corrupts the caravan position and token in a normal GM flow: the GM fixes the placement after players have plotted.
all.suggested_fix: In approve(), refuse or clear the plan when !validCourse(before.position, plan.course). Also, or instead, clear plan.course (and routeId) in caravan.place/unplace whenever the position changes.
all.rationale: 70: I could not refute this. The bug is real and sits on lines this diff added. In src/travel/index.ts, approve() (lines 313-323, new in the diff) only checks that a trip is not already running, that a position exists and that the course is non-empty. It then copies plan.course into the trip with `course: [...plan.course]` and never calls validCourse. validCourse runs only in setPlanHandler, when the plan is set. caravanService.place (src/caravan/index.ts, about 320-346) changes c.position and c.sceneId and leaves c.plan alone. It refuses only when c.trip is set, so moving the caravan between plotting and approval is allowed. Nothing else clears or re-checks the plan when the caravan moves. I searched src/caravan, src/canvas, the dropCanvasData hook and placeCaravanToken in src/ui/caravan-app.ts. The engine does not check adjacency either: moveToday (src/engine) steps from ctx.position straight to course[0..n] and only checks that each hex is passable. runDay then sets after.position = out.end and calls moveToken(before.sceneId, out.end), so the caravan and its token jump to the old plotted hexes, on whatever scene the caravan is on now. Two things limit how often this hits, which is why I did not score 75 or higher. First, the window is narrow: the GM has to move the caravan after players plot and before approval, because approve clears the plan and place is refused during a trip. Second, drawCourse draws a line from the new position to the stale course[0], so an attentive GM gets a visual hint. Still, re-placing the caravan after players plot is a plausible GM step, and the result corrupts the caravan's position.

all.title: Rest-day repair can push party funds negative after wages; the next day's wages then 'pay' a negative amount
all.description: engine.resolveDay grants a repair when ctx.funds >= REPAIR_COST (1000 cp), checked before wages. runDay first takes wages (after.funds -= paid) and then subtracts the repair cost unconditionally. Example: funds 1000 cp, wages 30 cp gives 970 - 1000 = -30 cp. On the next day, paid = Math.min(-30, wages) = -30, so funds go up, the card prints coinText(-30) (gp = Math.floor(-0.3) = -1, which gives garbage text), and the GM is whispered a wrong shortfall.
all.reason: Funds are a tracked resource, and negative funds give wrong coin text and wrong wage accounting in live play.
all.suggested_fix: Apply the repair only if after.funds >= out.repair.cost after wages (skip it and note why otherwise), or check wages + repair together in the engine. Clamp paid to Math.max(0, ...).
all.rationale:
55: I could not refute the mechanism, but it does not break any declared invariant, and it only triggers in a narrow window.

The bug is real and sits on new lines from this diff:
- src/engine/index.ts:338 grants a repair when `ctx.funds >= REPAIR_COST` (1000 cp). That check uses the funds from before wages are taken, and the wage total is computed on every activity, rest days included (engine line 317).
- src/travel/index.ts:220-224 takes wages first, clamped to `after.funds`.
- src/travel/index.ts:236 then subtracts `out.repair.cost` with no check, so funds go negative.
- The next day, `paid = Math.min(-30, wages)` is -30, so funds rise back to 0. The card prints `coinText(-30)`, which is "-1 gp -3 sp" (Math.floor of negative numbers). The GM is also whispered a shortfall of wages+30, which overstates it by 30 cp.
- The Caravan FUNDS tile would also show the negative value.

The one thing I could not confirm is the "invariant" framing. None of the four load-bearing invariants in CLAUDE.md covers non-negative funds. Invariant 4 (the last day step can be undone) is unaffected, because the funds are captured in the undo snapshot.

It only happens when all of these are true at once:
- it is a rest day;
- the wainwright role is filled;
- a vehicle is damaged;
- at least one traveller has a non-zero wage;
- funds are in the narrow band [1000, 1000 + daily wages), which is usually just a few tens of cp.

That makes it a real but uncommon edge case. The fix is small: subtract wages before checking the repair cost, or check again in runDay before line 236.

all.title: GM choosing a hidden route in the Travel window silently clears the course
all.description: For the GM, the route <select> lists Object.values(view.routes), where view is the full map, so routes unknown to the party appear too. The change handler looks the chosen id up in store.partyView(...).routes, which only holds routes with knownToParty. For a hidden route, route is null, course is [], and setPlan posts 'cleared the road', wiping any existing plotted course.
all.reason: A GM action in live play destroys the plan with no feedback.
all.suggested_fix: Look the route up in the same map the select was built from (store.getMap for the GM, partyView for players), or list only known routes for everyone.
all.rationale:
80: I tried to refute this and could not. The bug is real, it is on lines this diff added, and it triggers through a normal GM action.

1. For the GM, src/ui/travel-app.ts:79 builds `view` from `store.getMap(...)`, which is the full map. Line 127 lists `Object.values(view.routes)` and filters only on `courseAlong(...).length`, not on `knownToParty`. So any hidden route through the caravan's hex shows up in the dropdown, with no marker saying it is hidden.

2. The change handler at line 164 (new in this diff) looks up the chosen id in `store.partyView(...).routes`. In src/store/index.ts:234-236, `partyView` copies a route only `if (route.knownToParty)`. A hidden route's id therefore returns `undefined`.

3. `route` is falsy, so `course = []` and `routeId = null`. The handler then calls `travel.setPlan(...)` with the message "cleared the road".

4. `setPlanHandler` (src/travel/index.ts:280-296) has nothing to stop it. It refuses only during a trip, for an unknown activity, or for an invalid course, and an empty course passes. It overwrites `after.plan` with an empty course and records "<GM> cleared the road" as the last edit.

How it triggers: the GM draws a route left hidden from players (`knownToParty` false), the caravan sits on one of its hexes, the GM opens Travel, and picks that route. Any course already plotted is wiped, and the dropdown goes back to "Follow a known road…" with no warning.

The only things that soften it are the visible "cleared the road" note and that the GM can plot the course again. all.title: Undo puts back the whole CaravanState, so it also reverts roster, role and fund edits made after the day, and party funds drift from character purses
all.description: undo.capture snapshots the full CaravanState (`caravan: structuredClone(caravan)`). undo.undo then runs `store.setCaravan(snap.caravan)`, which replaces the live state. Players can still edit between Next Day and Undo, because deposit, withdraw, roster and role requests apply at once. Those edits get thrown away too. Fund moves are the worst case: the character's pf1 currency is written with `setCoins` and is not in the snapshot, while `c.funds` rolls back. Example: a player withdraws 50 gp after the day step, so the PC gains 50 gp and funds drop by 50 gp. The GM then clicks Undo and funds go back to the pre-day value. The 50 gp now exists twice. A deposit made in that gap disappears from both places.
all.reason: Invariant 4 and DESIGN §4.13 say the snapshot holds what the day changes (supplies, vehicle HP, funds, knowledge, position/token, plan, time). They also say roster, role and fund edits are not undoable. Restoring the whole object goes past the day's own changes and breaks the link between party funds and actor coins.
all.suggested_fix: Restore only the fields the day step writes: position, journeyDay, trip, and funds as a delta (funds = current - (after_day_funds - before_day_funds)). Alternatively, store before/after values for those fields and apply only the day's change. Leave travellers, vehicles, roles and plan as they are now. Another option is to clear the snapshot whenever a fund, roster or role request is applied.
all.rationale:
72: I could not refute this. The bug is real, on lines this diff rewrote, and gives a wrong result when its trigger occurs. The trigger needs a player to edit between Next Day and Undo, so I scored it below "hits in practice".

What the code does (src/ledger/index.ts, rewritten in 912eaa4):
- Line 55: capture stores `caravan: structuredClone(caravan)`, the whole CaravanState.
- Line 99: undo runs `store.setCaravan(snap.caravan)` with no merge, so the live roster, roles, seats, teams and `funds` all go back to their state before the day.
- Nothing clears or adjusts the snapshot after a later edit. The only callers of undo.* are in src/travel/index.ts: capture at line 210, recordTime at 261, undo at 369. None are in src/caravan/index.ts.

The fund edit that slips through: in src/caravan/index.ts:202-233, `funds()` applies at once. It writes the PC's pf1 currency with `pf1Adapter.setCoins(actor, next)` and changes `c.funds` with `save(c)`. The snapshot holds `c.funds` but not the character's coins. So:
- Withdraw 50 gp after the day, then Undo: `c.funds` goes back up and the PC keeps the 50 gp, so the money exists twice.
- Deposit after the day, then Undo: the coins leave the PC and the deposit is wiped from `c.funds`, so the money is lost.

Against the spec: DESIGN.md §4.13 limits the snapshot to what the day changes (supplies, vehicle HP, funds, knowledge, position and token, plan, time). It says roster, role and fund edits are not undoable. Restoring the whole object goes past that. The one ambiguity in my reading: "not undoable; the GM fixes them by hand" could be read as Undo simply not being the tool for those edits. Even so, silently creating or destroying coins is clearly wrong.

Why not higher: the trigger is narrow. A player has to roster/role/fund edit after Next Day and before the GM's Undo. Undo usually follows a mistaken day step right away, so this is plausible but not frequent. The predecessor ledger (15741e7) also restored the caravan whole per entry, but the current code is a new design on changed lines, so it is not exempt as pre-existing.

all.title: The GM's check of a setPlan course uses whatever scene the GM is viewing, not the caravan's scene
all.description: validCourse reads `canvas?.grid?.columns` and `canvas?.grid?.even` from the active GM's current canvas. The caravan's own scene (`c.sceneId`) is never consulted. If the GM is on a different scene (a square-grid dungeon, or a hex map with the other orientation or offset parity), adjacency is computed with the wrong offset rules. A course of non-adjacent hexes can then be accepted, and runDay later moves the caravan along it as if each step were adjacent. The opposite also happens: a valid player course is rejected. The client side has the same weakness. course.ts plotCourse only checks `canvas.grid.isHexagonal` and never checks `canvas.scene.id === c.sceneId`, so a player looking at another scene builds the chain with that scene's grid.
all.reason: Invariant 2 says the active GM's client must validate every request. Here the result of that check depends on which scene the GM happens to be looking at, so a malformed course can pass.
all.suggested_fix: Take columns and even from the caravan's scene (`game.scenes.get(before.sceneId)?.grid`, with the same viewed-vs-BaseGrid fallback used in caravan.gridFor). If that scene is not hexagonal, refuse the request. In plotCourse, refuse when the viewed scene is not the caravan's scene.
all.rationale:
50: The bug is real, but its practical effect is smaller than the finding says.

**What I confirmed**
- Lines 77-78 of `X:\Development\foundry-mods\hexploration-old\src\travel\index.ts` are new in this diff. The old travel controller had no `validCourse`.
- `validCourse` takes `columns` and `even` from the GM's current `canvas.grid`, not from the scene in `c.sceneId`.
- `setPlanHandler` (line 285) calls it with only `before.position`, so the scene the caravan is on never reaches the check.
- `engine.hexAdjacent` converts offset coordinates to cube coordinates using those two flags. With the wrong orientation or parity, two hexes can be judged adjacent when they are not, or the reverse.
- The rest of the code already handles this correctly elsewhere: `moveToken`, `ledger.caravanToken` and `caravan.sceneFor` all resolve `sceneId` through `game.scenes.get`. A scene's own `grid` object could have been read here the same way.
- On the client, `plotCourse` in `X:\Development\foundry-mods\hexploration-old\src\canvas\course.ts` only checks `canvas.grid.isHexagonal`. `chain()` uses `canvas.grid.getDirectPath` on whatever scene the player is viewing, and nothing checks `canvas.scene.id === c.sceneId`.

**Why it is weaker than claimed**
1. It only goes wrong when the GM is viewing a different scene whose grid rules differ from the caravan's map. Mostly that means the caravan map is a column-based (flat-top) or even-offset hex grid, while the GM is on a square, gridless or differently laid-out map. If the caravan map is odd-row hex, a square or gridless scene gives the same defaults (`columns` and `even` both false), so the check still comes out right.
2. An honest player who plots on the caravan's scene sends a course that is adjacent under the correct grid. The likely failure is therefore a valid plan being refused while the GM is on, say, a battle map. A malformed course getting accepted needs a hand-crafted request, or a player plotting on the wrong scene. In that second case the coordinates are meaningless whatever the validator does, so the root problem is the missing client-side scene check.
3. Invariant 2 is not really broken. The GM client still checks and performs every write; the check just gives a scene-dependent answer. That makes this a correctness bug rather than a broken invariant.
4. If a bad course does get through, `runDay` moves the caravan by skipping a hex or two. No hidden information leaks.

**Verdict:** real, on a changed line, and it can happen in play (a GM switching to an encounter map while the players plan). Most of the time the outcome is a refused plan, so I scored it as real but minor.

all.title: The knowledge snapshot and the day's knowledge write can target different scenes, so Undo may not restore map knowledge
all.description: capture stores `party: caravan.sceneId ? store.getPartyMap(caravan.sceneId) : null`. runDay writes knowledge to `before.sceneId ?? canvas?.scene?.id` (travel/index.ts:240). When the caravan has a position but `sceneId` is null, the day still raises knowledge on the viewed scene, but no snapshot was taken. Undo then skips the knowledge restore (`if (snap.sceneId && snap.party)`). That case occurs with migrated or partially set caravan state, since migrateCaravan sets sceneId to null when it is missing. The token is not affected because both sides already fall back to `canvas.scene`.
all.reason: Invariant 4 says each day step must snapshot everything it changes, map knowledge included. Here the day can write knowledge that Undo cannot put back.
all.suggested_fix: Work out the target scene once, as `before.sceneId ?? canvas.scene.id`. Pass it to undo.capture and use it for both the snapshot (sceneId and party) and the write. Or refuse to step the day when `sceneId` is null.
all.rationale:
35: The mismatch is real, and it is on new code. src/ledger/index.ts is new in this diff. Line 67 only snapshots knowledge when caravan.sceneId is set. runDay (src/travel/index.ts:240) writes knowledge to `before.sceneId ?? canvas?.scene?.id`. Undo skips the restore when snap.sceneId is null (ledger:96). So if position is set while sceneId is null and a scene is being viewed, the day changes knowledge that Undo cannot put back.

The state that triggers it is very hard to reach in practice:
- In the new code, `place` (caravan/index.ts:344-345) always sets position and sceneId together, and `unplace` (357-359) always clears both.
- `approve` (travel/index.ts:318) and runDay (200) both refuse to run without a position.
- runDay only changes position and leaves sceneId alone.
- migrateCaravan reads sceneId and position separately, but it only makes the bad pair from old saved data that already had it.

The only old path I found that wrote position without sceneId is 0.1.x travel/index.ts:503-504: `after.sceneId = canvas?.scene?.id ?? after.sceneId; after.position ??= plan.from`. That only happens if a muster ran while the GM had no scene open, which is unusual. The other route is hand-editing the caravan flag.

So the bug is real but a rare edge case. It does not hit in normal play: a migrated 0.1.x caravan that was placed with a scene, or any caravan placed in 0.2.x, has both fields set.
