all.title: GM-only writes run on any GM client, outside the active GM's write queue
all.description: gmWrite only checks `game.user?.isGM` and then calls the module-local `exclusive()` queue. The travel controller's day step, approve, stop and undo do the same through gmOnly. That queue exists separately in each browser. A second (assistant) GM can therefore read-modify-write the whole caravan JSON flag (place, updateTraveller, updateVehicle, Next Day, Undo) while the active GM's client is applying player requests. Whichever write lands second wipes out the first. Player edits, by contrast, go through `authority.isActiveGM()`.
all.reason: Invariant 2 says the active GM's client performs every world-state write. The new `edit()` path follows that rule, but the new gmWrite path does not, so writes from two GM clients are not serialized.
all.suggested_fix: Gate gmWrite and the travel GM actions on `authority.isActiveGM()`. A non-active GM can either send these actions to the active GM as requests (checking that the sender isGM) or be refused with a message naming the active GM.
all.rationale:
10: I'm refuting this as a regression. The behaviour existed before this diff and this change does not introduce it. At the base commit (15741e7), src/caravan/index.ts already had `gmWrite` that checked only `game.user?.isGM` and then called `exclusive()`, with the queue imported from ../travel at that point. src/travel/index.ts already had `gmOnly()` that checked only `game.user?.isGM`, and its day, approve and stop steps already ran through a module-local `exclusive` queue. The diff moved `exclusive` into src/caravan/index.ts at lines 28-34 and reshaped `gmWrite` at lines 257-267, but the logic is the same. The new `edit()` path, which routes through `authority.isActiveGM()`, covers only player-requestable edits, and those were already routed through the active GM before.

The cross-client race is real in principle. Each browser keeps its own queue, and the caravan flag is read, changed and written back whole. But it needs two GM clients writing the caravan within the same round trip, for example an assistant GM placing the caravan or pressing Next Day while the active GM is applying a player request. That is rare in normal play, which usually has a single GM. It is a pre-existing design gap against the active-GM-writes rule (invariant 2), not a correctness bug introduced on the changed lines.

all.title: Players' seat, driver and team changes are applied without whispering the GM
all.description: addActor, removeActor and funds whisper the GM when a player is the sender (`if (!user?.isGM) await whisperGM(...)`). setSeat, setDriver and setTeam apply the change and return with no whisper. DESIGN §4.13 lists seat, drive and pull as roster edits that are 'applied at once; the GM is whispered, since it changes daily use'. These edits change the caravan's pace, cargo and driver checks, and the GM gets no notice before the next day step.
all.reason: This part of the GM-as-sole-authority operator model (§4.13, invariant 2) depends on the GM being told about player roster changes that apply without approval. These three handlers skip that step.
all.suggested_fix: After a successful save in setSeat, setDriver and setTeam, add the same `if (!user?.isGM) await whisperGM(...)` line used in addActor and removeActor, describing the change (for example "X now drives the Wagon").
all.rationale:
70: The finding is real, and it sits on lines this diff changed. The handlers were rewritten in this diff: setSeat, setDriver and setTeam are new + lines in `git diff 15741e7...HEAD -- src/caravan/index.ts`. The old file was GM-only and ledger-based.

DESIGN.md §4.13 (lines 264-265) says that when players edit the roster with actors they own ("add, remove, seat, drive, pull"), the edits are "applied at once; the GM is whispered, since it changes daily use".

In src/caravan/index.ts the code only partly follows that:
- addActor (line 122), removeActor (line 139) and funds (lines 228-231) all call `if (!user?.isGM) await whisperGM(...)`.
- setSeat (lines 143-152), setDriver (lines 154-171) and setTeam (lines 173-185) end with `return save(c)` and never whisper.

This does trigger in practice. Every player edit made in the Caravan sheet goes through edit(), then authority.send(), then the GM handler, then run(..., user), where user is not the GM. So the GM gets no message when a player re-seats someone, swaps a driver or changes a team. No test checks whispers for these handlers (test/integration/roster.test.ts has none), and no ADR or DECISIONS entry exempts them.

Why I scored below 80: this breaks a DESIGN requirement, not strictly the declared invariant. Invariant 2 (the GM is the only writer) still holds, because the GM's client validates and applies every change. The harm is only that the GM is not told. The change is visible on the shared caravan state and sheet, and the GM can fix it by hand. So it is a verified spec gap of moderate importance, not an invariant breach.

all.title: Undo restores the whole CaravanState, so roster, role, fund and plan edits made after the day are lost
all.description: undo.capture snapshots the full caravan (structuredClone(caravan), line 55), and undo() writes it back with store.setCaravan(snap.caravan). Nothing clears the snapshot when the caravan is edited later. Example: after Day 3 a player deposits 50 gp. caravan.funds takes the coins off the character's sheet and adds 5000 cp to c.funds. If the GM then undoes Day 3, funds go back to the pre-day value. The 50 gp is gone from the party funds and stays gone from the character, and nothing reports it. Travellers, vehicles, roles and the plan added or changed after the day are rolled back the same way.
all.reason: DESIGN §4.13 says roster, role, fund and plan edits are not undoable, so undo should leave them alone. Restoring an absolute snapshot erases them, and in the funds case the coins vanish from the world.
all.suggested_fix: Restore only the fields the day changed (position, journeyDay, trip, and funds as a delta: current funds + wages paid + repair cost). Or clear the lastDay snapshot whenever a caravan edit is applied, so Undo is no longer offered once later edits exist.
all.rationale: 75: I could not refute this finding. src/ledger/index.ts was rewritten in this diff (83+/71-). Line 55 snapshots structuredClone(caravan), and line 99 writes it back unconditionally with store.setCaravan(snap.caravan). The snapshot is only replaced by the next capture() or cleared by undo() itself. No roster, role, fund or plan edit in src/caravan/index.ts clears or patches it, so the Undo button stays up (travel-app.ts:101) after those edits. The funds case checks out: caravan.funds (caravan/index.ts:202-224) takes the coins off the actor's sheet and does c.funds += cp. A later undo puts c.funds back to the pre-day value while the character sheet stays debited, so the coins are lost and nothing reports it. Even so, overwriting edits made after the day goes against "Roster, role, fund and plan edits are not undoable", and the coin loss is a real error, not just a matter of interpretation. It needs a specific order of events (day, then a player edit, then the GM presses Undo), but setting roles or moving funds between days is a normal part of play. Real, important and hits in practice; I have not seen it at runtime, so I put it at 75 rather than higher.

all.title: Rest-day repair cost is taken after wages, so party funds can go negative
all.description: engine.resolveDay grants a repair only if ctx.funds >= REPAIR_COST (engine line 338), and ctx.funds is read before wages. runDay first pays wages (after.funds -= paid, line 222), then always runs after.funds -= out.repair.cost (line 236). With 1000 cp in funds and 200 cp of daily wages on a rest day, funds end at -200 cp. The card says the repair was paid and nothing warns. The negative balance is then saved and shown.
all.reason: Funds are never meant to go below zero (withdraw and wage payment both guard against it). Nothing reports the overdraft, and later deposits silently fill the hole.
all.suggested_fix: Check after.funds >= out.repair.cost after paying wages, and skip the repair (or have the engine count wages before deciding on a repair) when funds are short. Clamp at 0 and whisper the GM if the repair can't be paid.
all.rationale: 72: I could not refute it. The bug is real, and it sits on lines this diff added. In src/engine/index.ts:338 the engine grants a repair only when ctx.funds >= REPAIR_COST (1000 cp), and ctx.funds is the balance before the day's costs. Wages are summed from ctx.eaters at line 317 for every activity, rest days included. In src/travel/index.ts the code first takes the wages (lines 221-222: paid = min(funds, wages)). Then at line 236 it subtracts out.repair.cost with no check at all. So funds of 1000 cp and 200 cp of wages on a rest day end at -200 cp. That -200 is saved by store.setCaravan(after), and the card still shows "Repairs: +N HP ... (10 gp)" with no warning. This breaks the funds rule in DESIGN.md:233-234: when funds fall short, only what can be paid is paid and the GM is whispered. The wage code follows that rule; the repair code does not. Two things keep the score below 80. The bug needs a Wainwright on a rest day, a damaged vehicle, and funds between 1000 cp and 1000 cp plus that day's wages, which is a narrow window. And the damage is a wrong balance, not a crash. To fix it, check funds after wages in runDay (or have the engine compare against funds minus wages), and skip the repair or whisper the GM when funds are short.

all.title: Deposit/withdraw writes the character's coins before the caravan save, with no rollback
all.description: In apply.funds, pf1Adapter.setCoins(actor, next) runs first and save(c) second. If store.setCaravan throws (caravan actor deleted or unset between checks, permission error, flag write failure), run() turns the error into {ok:false, code:'failed'}. The character update has already happened by then. A failed deposit removes the coins from the character without adding them to party funds. A failed withdraw gives the coins to the character without taking them from funds.
all.reason: The user sees a generic failure and assumes nothing changed, but one half of the transfer already went through. Money is lost or duplicated without notice.
all.suggested_fix: Save the caravan first and update the character second, restoring the previous funds if setCoins fails. Or wrap both writes and on failure put the character's original purse back before returning the error.
all.rationale:
40: The defect is real, but it should rarely fire in play. The code is on a line this diff added. In src/caravan/index.ts lines 226-227, apply.funds awaits pf1Adapter.setCoins(actor, next) (an actor.update) and only then calls save(c), which calls store.setCaravan. There is no compensating write. run() at lines 237-245 catches any error and returns {ok:false, code:'failed'}, so a throw from setCaravan leaves the character's coins changed while the party funds stay the same.

I could not find a common way to make it fire.
(1) requireGM() in setCaravan always passes. run() only executes on the active GM, either directly through edit() when authority.isActiveGM() is true, or through the authority handler.
(2) requireCaravanActor() can only throw if the caravan actor is deleted or the caravanActor setting is cleared during the await of setCoins. run() checks getCaravanActor() inside the same exclusive() queue just before this, and getCaravanActor falls back to any actor of the caravan type. So this needs a manual delete by the GM in a window of a few milliseconds.
(3) setFlag is a GM write to an actor the GM owns, so it fails only on a server or socket error or a rejected update. That is possible but uncommon.
setCoins itself is one atomic actor.update, so it cannot half-apply.

The consequence, when it does fire, is silent loss or duplication of money, so it is worth a fix: write the caravan first, or restore the purse in a catch block. But it only triggers on rare race or infrastructure failures, not on normal inputs. That puts it between 25 (maybe) and 50 (real but minor), not at 75 (hits in practice).

all.title: "Ask to stop" shows success even when the request failed
all.description: askStop awaits authority.send({type:'askStop'}) but ignores the RequestResult and always shows "Asked the GM to stop the caravan." authority.send returns {ok:false, error:'No GM connected'} when no GM is online or the reply times out, so the player believes the GM was asked when nobody was told.
all.reason: The return value is dropped. The player gets a false confirmation while the caravan keeps travelling.
all.suggested_fix: const res = await authority.send(...); if (!res.ok) return toast(res.error ?? "Couldn't reach the GM.", "warn"); and show the success toast only after that check.
all.rationale:
60: The bug is real, and the diff adds the code (src/ui/travel-app.ts:66-70). The askStop action runs `await authority.send({ type: "askStop" })`, throws away the RequestResult, and then always calls `toast("Asked the GM to stop the caravan.")`. In src/authority/index.ts:58-76, `send` never throws. It returns `{ ok: false, error: "No GM connected" }` in two cases: when `game.users.activeGM` is missing, and when the 10-second reply timeout fires. A handler exception, such as whisperGM failing, also comes back as `{ ok: false }` from `handle()`. The `attempt()` wrapper in src/ui/html.ts:24 only catches thrown errors. So every failure path ends with the success toast. Other actions in the same file, such as `activity`, do check `res.ok` and warn, so this one is inconsistent with them.

Why the score is moderate rather than high: the stated impact, "the caravan keeps travelling", is overstated in the most common failure case. When no GM is connected, the day cannot advance, because only the GM client runs nextDay and travelAll, so the caravan is not actually moving. The timeout case, where a GM is listed but does not reply, is rarer. What is left is a misleading confirmation toast on a players-only button. It is a real UX and correctness slip, but it does little harm in practice. The fix is trivial: check `res.ok` and show `toast(res.error, "warn")` when it fails.

all.title: Missing or deleted encounter table is treated as "no encounter", and Travel all keeps going
all.description: encounterText calls fromUuid(table). A deleted or mistyped table resolves to null, so results is [] and text is "". lastEncounter is then false, and Travel all does not stop. The GM's whisper (lines 267-270) prints only the d20 total: the 'No encounter table' note appears only when table is null, not when the table is set but can't be found. Errors thrown during lookup are only logged to the console.
all.reason: A broken table reference hides every encounter in that region with no sign to the GM, and Travel all runs past days that should have stopped it.
all.suggested_fix: When table is set but fromUuid returns null or getResultsForRoll is missing or throws, return a sentinel such as {missing:true}. Whisper the GM that the encounter table can't be found, and set lastEncounter = true so Travel all stops.
all.rationale:
45: The mechanism is real and sits on lines this diff changed, but it does not break any declared invariant.

What holds up: src/travel/index.ts:125-134 (encounterText, new in this diff) returns "" when fromUuid gives null, because `t?.getResultsForRoll?.(total) ?? []` yields []. Line 266 then sets `lastEncounter = !!table && !isNothing("")`, which is false. travelAll (lines 343-354, also new) checks only lastEncounter, so it keeps going. The whisper at lines 267-270 prints the "No encounter table" note only when the table is null. A table that is set but can't be found shows only the d20 total with no warning. The table field is free text (src/canvas/painter.ts:218, `str(...).trim()`), and migrate.ts:65 copies old strings across unchecked, so a mistyped or deleted UUID can really happen.

Why the score stays low: under the invariant lens, nothing is violated. Invariant 1 (hidden truth) is not leaked. If anything, the failure hides more. Invariants 2 (GM is the only writer), 3 (pure engine) and 4 (undoable last day step) are untouched. The silent null and console-only error handling are also not new: the old encounter() at 15741e7 lines 238-245 had the same `table?.getResultsForRoll?.(total) ?? []` and console.error. This diff only adds the Travel all stop behaviour on top. The GM still gets a whisper with the total every day, so it is not fully invisible. It also needs a broken table reference, which is unusual for a GM using the region form.

Verdict: a real robustness and UX gap (the GM should be warned when a table can't be found), but minor, and not an invariant violation.

all.title: Clear course and plot Cancel ignore the setPlan result
all.description: clearCourse runs void travel.setPlan(...) and never looks at the result. course.ts line 94 (the Cancel action) does the same and then calls stopPlotting() anyway. If the GM refuses the plan (a trip is underway, no GM connected, invalid course), the user gets no feedback. With Cancel the old course isn't restored while the UI acts as if it was. Other setPlan callers in the same files do check res.ok and toast.
all.reason: The return value is dropped, so a refused plan change looks like it succeeded.
all.suggested_fix: Wrap both calls in attempt(async () => { const res = await travel.setPlan(...); if (!res.ok) toast(res.error ?? 'Refused', 'warn'); }), the same as the activity and route handlers.
all.rationale: 50: The finding is real, but it's minor. Both lines are new in this diff: course.ts is a new file, and the clearCourse action at travel-app.ts:59 was added. Both drop the RequestResult. travel.setPlan returns authority.send(...), which resolves to {ok:false} without throwing in three cases: (a) no active GM, or a reply timeout, giving "No GM connected"; (b) setPlanHandler refuses because a trip is underway; (c) validCourse fails. These paths trigger in practice. For Cancel (course.ts:94), a player starts plotting, the GM then approves a trip or moves the caravan, so `before` is no longer a valid chain from the new position, or the GM disconnects. The player presses Cancel, the refusal is silent and stopPlotting() still runs, so the hint closes as if the old course came back. For Clear (travel-app.ts:59), a player whose GM has dropped gets no feedback, and because this call isn't wrapped in attempt(), a throw would also be an unhandled rejection. The other setPlan callers (the activity action, the route select, and send() in course.ts) do check res.ok and warn, so this is an inconsistency. The impact is limited. Nothing is corrupted, because the GM never applied the change. The store-driven re-render and drawCourse still show the true course, so the user can see it wasn't cleared or restored. Clear is only rendered when there is no trip. With no GM connected, the earlier plot clicks would already have warned. So it is a real, reachable UX gap, but only on edge-case paths and with no damage to state.

all.title: Undo silently skips supplies, tokens and vehicles it can't resolve, then reports success
all.description: undo() restores through optional chaining: fromUuidSync(s.containerUuid)?.updateContainerContents?.(...), fromUuidSync(s.itemUuid)?.update?.(...), fromUuidSync(snap.token.uuid)?.update?.(...). It skips vehicles when a is null. Any target that no longer resolves is skipped without a word, and the caller still shows "Undid Day N." Also, capture (line 64) stores hp 0 for a vehicle actor that didn't resolve at capture time, so if it resolves at undo time, undo sets its HP to 0.
all.reason: The GM is told the day was undone while supply quantities, the token position or vehicle HP were not restored. That breaks invariant 4 without any sign.
all.suggested_fix: Collect the snapshot entries that fail to resolve and either refuse the undo or return a warning listing what couldn't be restored. At capture, leave unresolved vehicles out of the snapshot instead of storing hp 0.
all.rationale:
40: The code matches the description, and these lines are new in this diff. At src/ledger/index.ts:87, 89 and 97, undo() restores through optional chaining (`?.updateContainerContents?.`, `?.update?.`). At line 94 it skips a vehicle when `a` is null. It then still returns snap.label, and travel/index.ts:370 shows "Undid Day N." Line 64 does store hp 0 for a vehicle that didn't resolve at capture. So the silent partial undo is real.

It rarely triggers in practice, though. A snapshot covers only the most recent day, and the day step itself never deletes anything. Supplies are clamped to 0 through store.setSupplyQuantity, not deleted. Vehicles are only HP-updated. The token is only moved. So targets that capture recorded still resolve at undo, unless the GM deletes or re-parents a supply item, deletes the vehicle actor, or deletes the caravan token between the day step and pressing Undo. That is an unusual manual action, and undo is normally pressed right away.

The hp-0 case at line 64 needs a vehicle link that was dangling at capture and then starts resolving at undo. That means re-creating an actor with the same UUID, for example a keepId import, which is very unlikely. Also, the old ledger code (revert) used the same `fromUuidSync(...)?.update` silent-skip pattern, so this is a carried-over design choice rather than a new regression.

Verdict: real but a minor robustness gap with no warning (it should warn when a target is missing). It is not a common correctness failure.

all.title: approve() doesn't re-check the stored course against the caravan's current position
all.description: The course is validated only when setPlan is called. caravan.place() moves the caravan (allowed while there's no trip) but leaves plan.course as it was. approve() then copies the old course into trip.course without calling validCourse. engine.moveToday doesn't check that course[0] is next to position, so the next day moves the caravan straight to the first hexes of the old course: it jumps across the map with no error.
all.reason: An out-of-date plan is accepted as valid, and the caravan teleports instead of the GM being told the course no longer starts at the caravan.
all.suggested_fix: In approve(), check validCourse(before.position, plan.course) for travel plans and warn and refuse if it fails. Also clear plan.course in caravan.place() when the position changes.
all.rationale:
60: The bug is real and sits on code this diff rewrote, but I scored it as a moderate correctness bug, not a broken invariant. Mechanism (all checked in the code):
- X:\Development\foundry-mods\hexploration-old\src\travel\index.ts:285: setPlanHandler checks the course with validCourse(before.position, req.course), and that is the only check.
- X:\Development\foundry-mods\hexploration-old\src\caravan\index.ts:319-347: caravan.place refuses only when a trip is active. With no trip it sets c.position (and sceneId) and never touches c.plan. The plan therefore keeps its course, still tied to the old position.
- index.ts:313-324: approve() checks only for an active trip, a position and an empty course. It then copies plan.course into trip.course without calling validCourse.
- X:\Development\foundry-mods\hexploration-old\src\engine\index.ts:127-147: moveToday only checks that course[0] is passable. It never checks that course[0] is next to position. So the next runDay sets after.position = out.end (index.ts:252) somewhere along the old course, and moveToken moves the token there. The caravan jumps across the map with no error.
- Nothing else catches it. The UI's ready flag (travel-app.ts:144) only checks that a course exists. drawCourse (course.ts:133-136) draws a straight line from the new position to the old first hex, which the GM may or may not notice. Re-sending the plan via the activity tab (travel-app.ts:48) would fail, which supports the bug.

Why not higher:
- It only triggers when the GM moves the caravan after a plan is set but before approving it, for example fixing a misplaced token or placing it on the next scene while a plan is pending. That is plausible but not the main path, since approve and arrival both leave the plan empty.
- On the invariant lens it does not break a declared invariant. Invariant 2 (the GM validates every request) was met at request time, and approve is the GM's own action, not a player request. This is a correctness bug, not an invariant violation.

all.title: An invalid rations/water multiplier is silently saved as 1
all.description: rulesFromForm's mult() returns 1 for any input that is empty, not a number, or negative. Typing "1,5" (comma decimal), "x2" or "-1" in the region or map water multiplier silently saves 1, and the GM sees "Map defaults saved." / the region is saved. DC mods in the same form throw a validation error that is caught and shown as a notification, so only the multipliers lose bad input without telling the GM.
all.reason: Bad input is replaced by a default with no error, so desert water needs (for example) quietly drop back to normal.
all.suggested_fix: Return 1 only when the field is empty. Otherwise throw an Error naming the field ("Water multiplier must be a number of at least 0"), so the existing try/catch shows it the same way as dcMods errors.
all.rationale: 45: The finding is real, and the line was changed in this diff, but it is minor and mostly carried over from the old code. src/canvas/painter.ts:212-216 (new in 912eaa4) reads the rations and water fields with `mult`, which returns 1 whenever the text is empty, not a finite number, or negative. Both callers then save without telling the GM: saveMapDefaults shows "Map defaults saved." (line 253) and saveRegion just saves (lines 272-294). Only parseDcMods throws, and that error is caught and shown at lines 244/278. So it does trigger. Typing "-1" in a water multiplier field saves 1 with no warning. "1,5" and "x2" never reach the code as text: the fields are <input type="number"> (line 398), and Chromium/Electron sets .value to "" for unparseable number input. onFieldChange (line 613) stores "", and mult turns that into 1. That limits the fix: mult cannot tell a blank field from a bad one by the string alone, so it would need el.validity.badInput. The old code (15741e7 lines 272/316) did `Number(str("md.water")) || 1`, which also quietly turned bad input into 1, and turned 0 into 1 as well. The new code is stricter than that (it keeps 0, rejects negatives) and adds the same fallback for the new rations field. The silent fallback is not a new regression. What is new is that the DC mods field in the same form now reports bad input while the multipliers do not. The fields are seeded with "1", so the GM only hits this by typing a negative number or a comma decimal. Real but minor UX validation gap.

all.title: An unresolvable vehicle actor is reported as "wrecked" (hp 0) instead of missing
all.description: vehicleInfos falls back to {hp: 0, maxHp: 0} when fromUuidSync can't resolve a linked vehicle (actor deleted, bad UUID). engine.vehicleBlock then reports "<name> is wrecked" and the trip is blocked. The real cause, a missing linked actor, never shows, and the cargo weight also defaults to 0.

all.suggested_fix: Mark unresolved vehicles (e.g. missing: true) and have pace/vehicleBlock report "<name> can't be found; re-link or remove it", or drop them from the roster with a GM warning.
all.rationale: 50: The finding holds up, but it only fires in an edge case. src/travel/context.ts is a new file in this diff, and on line 43 a vehicle actor that cannot be resolved gets {hp: 0, maxHp: 0}. In src/engine/index.ts:79-84, vehicleBlock checks the driver first, then the team, then `hp <= 0`, which returns "<name> is wrecked". The UI makes the inconsistency clear: src/ui/caravan-app.ts:376 guards with `info.maxHp > 0 && info.hp <= 0`, so the Caravan sheet does not show "Wrecked" while the engine's blocked message says it is. I found no deleteActor hook or pruning that would stop a dangling vehicle link. It needs the GM to delete a linked vehicle actor in the middle of a campaign, which is uncommon. If the driver or team actors were deleted as well, the earlier checks show a different message. So the wrong result is real (a misleading block reason) but minor and infrequent.

all.title: Undo snapshot stores the whole CaravanState, so undo also rolls back roster, role and fund edits made after the day
all.description: `Snapshot.caravan` is a full `structuredClone(caravan)`, and `undo()` writes it back wholesale with `store.setCaravan(snap.caravan)` (line 99). DESIGN §4.13 says a day snapshot covers what the day changes (supplies, vehicle HP, funds, knowledge, position/token, plan, time) and that roster, role and fund edits are not undoable. Because the field's type is the whole aggregate, any edit made between Next Day and Undo gets reverted with it. Funds are the worst case: a player deposits 50 gp after the day step, which `pf1Adapter.setCoins` removes from the character, then the GM undoes the day. `c.funds` goes back to its pre-deposit value and the coins are gone from both places. Travellers added or removed, seats, drivers and roles revert silently the same way.
all.reason: The data structure is broader than the contract it implements, and it breaks invariant 4's scope. It can destroy player coin, which is not recoverable from the snapshot.
all.suggested_fix: Narrow the snapshot type to the fields the day writes, e.g. `caravan: Pick<CaravanState, 'position' | 'journeyDay' | 'trip' | 'plan'>` plus a funds delta (`fundsSpent: number`, wages + repair). On undo, merge those into the current `store.getCaravan()` instead of replacing it, and add the spent funds back rather than restoring an absolute value.
all.rationale:
75: I could not refute this. src/ledger/index.ts is entirely new in this diff; the old file was a different ledger-entry design. Line 55 stores `structuredClone(caravan)`, the whole CaravanState: travellers, vehicles, roles, funds, sceneId, position, journeyDay, plan and trip. Line 99 then writes it back wholesale with `store.setCaravan(snap.caravan)`. Nothing clears the snapshot when a roster, role or fund edit happens. The only things that clear it are undo, which writes null at line 100, and the next day's `capture`, which overwrites it. `caravan.funds` (src/caravan/index.ts:202-233) has no trip or undo guard. It moves real coins through `pf1Adapter.setCoins` and then saves `c.funds`.

Concrete failure:
1. The GM runs Next Day. `capture` records funds F, then wages are deducted.
2. A player deposits 50 gp. `setCoins` takes 50 gp from the character and funds become F - wages + 5000 cp.
3. The GM clicks Undo and funds return to F. The 50 gp is gone from both the character and the party funds.

A withdrawal in step 2 does the reverse: the coins are duplicated. Roster, role and seat edits made in between are also reverted silently. This contradicts DESIGN §4.13 ("Roster, role, fund and plan edits are not undoable"), even though the same section lists party funds among what the day changes. Restoring an absolute funds value cannot tell the day's wage and repair debits apart from later player deposits.

It needs an edit between Next Day and Undo, which is plausible at the table (for example, players topping up after a "Wages short" whisper). That is what keeps it below certainty.

all.title: Repair affordability ignores the same day's wages; party funds can go negative
all.description: `resolveDay` grants a rest-day repair when `ctx.funds >= REPAIR_COST`, and it returns `wages` and `repair.cost` as two separate charges. `runDay` (src/travel/index.ts:320-336) pays wages first (`after.funds -= paid`, capped at funds), then subtracts `out.repair.cost` with no check. Example: 1,000 cp in funds and one trained hireling at 30 cp/day on a Rest day. Wages take 30 cp, the repair takes 1,000 cp, and `CaravanState.funds` ends at -30. The UI renders that through `cpText` and the withdraw guard (`c.funds < cp`). Nothing in the type or the contract says which charge has priority or that the two share one budget.
all.reason: Units and budget agreement across engine/travel: the engine checks a precondition against a value the controller has already changed. `funds` is documented as a cp balance and is assumed to be non-negative everywhere else.
all.suggested_fix: In the engine, check `ctx.funds - wagesDue >= REPAIR_COST`, using the wages it computes a few lines earlier. Or have `DayOutcome` carry one `spend` breakdown that the controller applies atomically, and clamp in `runDay`.
all.rationale:
60: I could not refute it. The bug is real and sits on lines this diff adds, but it only fires in a narrow funds window.

What the code shows:

all.title: `Pace.blocked` means 'a vehicle can't move' but Travel all reads it as 'the caravan can't continue', ending multi-day Explore after day 1
all.description: The engine's `pace()` sets `blocked` whenever any vehicle is undriven, under-teamed, wrecked or overloaded, whatever the activity. `preview()` returns it unchanged when not travelling (engine line 235), and `runDay` only refuses on `blocked` for travel trips. `travelAll` breaks on `out.pace.blocked` for every activity. A 3-day Explore with an undriven or short-teamed wagon runs one day, then Travel all stops silently with the trip still active. The `Pace` type documents `blocked` as 'why the caravan can't move', which is only true for a travel day.
all.reason: Field semantics differ between producer and consumer. The same field means different things depending on activity, and the type has no way to show that.
all.suggested_fix: Use `blocked` only for movement. In `preview()`, return `blocked: null` when `!travelling`, or add a separate `vehicleIssues: string[]` field. Then gate the `travelAll` break on `trip.activity === 'travel'`.
all.rationale:
75: I could not refute this. The finding is real and sits on code this diff adds. The only thing wrong is the line number: the check is at src/travel/index.ts:351, not 451, because the file is 398 lines long. The whole file is new in this diff, and the line `if (out.pace.blocked) break;` appears as an added line in the diff of travelAll.

How it triggers, traced through the code:
1. engine pace() (src/engine/index.ts:87-102) sets `blocked ??= vehicleBlock(v)` for any vehicle, whatever the activity. vehicleBlock returns a reason when a vehicle has no driver, has fewer draft animals than it needs, is at hp<=0, or carries more than twice its cargo capacity.
2. preview() (engine:216-235) only replaces blocked with the move result when `travelling`. Otherwise it returns `pace: p`, so `blocked` is still set on Explore, Rest and Forage days.
3. resolveDay passes `pv.pace` through to the outcome (engine:382).
4. runDay (travel:204) only refuses when `trip.activity === "travel" && preview.pace.blocked`. An Explore day therefore resolves normally. exploreDays goes up by one and the trip stays active while `exploreDays + 1 < exploreNeeded` (engine:355).
5. travelAll (travel:344-352) breaks on `out.pace.blocked` for every activity, and shows no notification.

Concrete case: the caravan explores a hex that needs at least 2 days on EXPLORE_TABLE. One wagon has no driver assigned (nobody needs to drive while exploring), or it was wrecked by earlier wear, or it is short of draft animals. Travel all runs day 1, then quietly stops with the trip still underway.

The same thing happens on multi-day Rest. These states are plausible in normal play, because a wrecked or undriven wagon is exactly why a group might stop to explore or rest.

I did not score it higher because the impact is limited. Nothing gets corrupted. The GM sees Travel all stop early and has to press Next day or Travel all again. It hits often enough to matter, but it is not severe.

all.title: Role skills are bare parent ids ('pro', 'crf'), so any Profession or Craft rank qualifies, not the profession DESIGN names
all.description: `RoleDef.skills` is `string[]` of pf1 parent ids. DESIGN §4.5 names specific subskills: Profession (guide/scout/hunter/driver/wainwright/cartographer/cook) and Craft (carpentry). `pf1Adapter.bestSkill` (src/pf1/index.ts:212-213) expands 'pro'/'crf' to every subskill the actor has and takes the highest mod. A character with Profession (sailor) +14 rolls it as Navigator, Driver, Wainwright and so on, and Craft (alchemy) counts for the Wainwright. The data structure can't express 'Profession (guide)', so the daily auto-roll and the Caravan sheet's role bonus column both use the wrong skill.
all.reason: The type can't encode the rule it is meant to carry, which silently inflates every role's bonus for characters with any high Profession or Craft.
all.suggested_fix: Model skills as `{ id: string; sub?: string }[]` (e.g. `{ id: 'pro', sub: 'guide' }`). In `bestSkill`, match a subskill by its `name` (case-insensitive) instead of taking any subskill. A bare parent with no `sub` keeps today's behaviour for Survival, Perception and so on.
all.rationale:
45: The mismatch is real, but it is not a regression and it is small.

- **What the finding gets right.** The new DESIGN.md §4.5 (lines 182-188) names specific subskills: Profession (guide/scout/hunter/driver/wainwright/cartographer/cook) and Craft (carpentry). ROLE_DEFS in src/types.ts:163-171 lists only the bare 'pro'/'crf' ids. pf1Adapter.bestSkill (src/pf1/index.ts:209-216) loops over every subSkill of a SUBSKILL_PARENTS id and keeps the highest mod. So Profession (sailor) or Craft (alchemy) does qualify for every role. Both the travel auto-roll (src/travel/index.ts:148) and the Caravan role column (src/ui/caravan-app.ts:358) use it.
- **Line 160 did not change.** The RoleDef `skills: string[]` line with that same comment exists at 15741e7:src/types.ts:152.
- **The behaviour is old.** The pre-diff code in src/engine/index.ts:29-89 already used the same skill lists (['sur','pro'], ['pro','crf'], and so on), and bestSkill's subskill expansion is identical before and after. This diff only moved the role defs into types.ts and added the specific Profession names to DESIGN (`git show 15741e7:DESIGN.md` has no 'profession' anywhere). So the doc and the code now disagree, but nothing in the code got worse.
- **The narrow rule is hard to build.** pf1 Profession/Craft subskills use generic keys (pro1, crf1…) with a free-text name. Matching 'guide' would mean fuzzy name matching, so the permissive approach is a plausible deliberate simplification and not a logic error.
- **Impact.** It does fire for any character with a high off-theme Profession/Craft, inflating one role's bonus. That is a rules-fidelity issue in a table-assist tool, not a crash or wrong math.

Verdict: real spec/code divergence, minor, pre-existing behaviour.

all.title: Doubling penalty is applied in the roll, added back by the controller, then subtracted by the engine
all.description: `rollSkill(actor, skill, check.penalty)` puts `-${penalty}[Doubling]` into the pf1 roll (src/pf1/index.ts:237), and `rollChecks` adds the penalty back (`total + check.penalty`) so `resolveDay` can subtract it again (`raw - c.penalty + c.bonus`). The Pf1Api contract says the result has the penalty applied, while `EngineApi.resolveDay` expects totals without it. The two layers' units disagree, and travel patches the difference by hand. If pf1 ignores or renames the `bonus` option, the add-back turns into a +penalty and the doubling penalty silently disappears. The stated reason for in-roll labelling is a visible chat label, but `chatMessage: false` means nobody sees it.
all.reason: The value means different things at each layer boundary, and correctness depends on an unverified pf1 option being honoured.
all.suggested_fix: Roll without the penalty (drop the `penalty` parameter from `Pf1Api.rollSkill`, or pass 0) and let the engine be the only place it is applied. Document `totals` as 'raw d20 + skill, no penalty' in both contracts.
all.rationale: 25: The finding cites src/travel/index.ts:253, but that line is trip bookkeeping. The code it describes is in rollChecks at src/travel/index.ts:149-153, which the diff did add. The new line is `totals[check.id] = total + check.penalty; // the engine applies the penalty itself`. The arithmetic is correct. pf1 rolls d20+mod-penalty, the controller adds the penalty back, and engine resolveDay (src/engine/index.ts:281) computes `raw - c.penalty + c.bonus`, so the doubling penalty is applied exactly once. This holds as long as pf1 honours the `bonus` option on actor.rollSkill. That option line (`options.bonus = \`-${penalty}[Doubling]\``) predates the diff, and the old engine already relied on it ('The doubling penalty was already applied to the submitted total by the roller'). As far as I know, pf1 v10/v11 rollSkill supports a `bonus` option, so the failure is hypothetical. The failure described is also slightly wrong: if `bonus` were ignored, the net result would be raw (the penalty is lost), not an extra +penalty. The finding is right on two points. The contract comment in src/contracts.ts:139 says the penalty is applied while the engine expects a raw total, so the units differ between layers. And with `chatMessage: false` the [Doubling] label is never shown, which makes the in-roll penalty a pointless round-trip. That is a code smell or simplification point (pass 0 or drop the penalty argument), not a correctness bug. It breaks none of the four invariants in DESIGN.md section 5: hidden truth, GM as the only writer, pure and seeded engine, undoable day step. It does not cause wrong results in practice.

all.title: Engine and Caravan sheet disagree on 'wrecked' for vehicles with maxHp 0
all.description: `vehicleBlock` treats `v.hp <= 0` as wrecked with no guard. `vehicleInfos` sets `hp: 0, maxHp: 0` when the vehicle actor can't be resolved, and `pf1Adapter.vehicleHp` returns 0/0 for a vehicle actor whose HP isn't set up. The Caravan sheet's vehicle card (src/ui/caravan-app.ts:375-376) guards with `info.maxHp > 0 &&`, so it shows no Wrecked or Broken warning, while the engine blocks travel with '<name> is wrecked'. The broken/wrecked predicates live in two modules with different definitions.
all.reason: A derived state is defined twice and the definitions don't match, so the sheet tells the GM the vehicle is fine while Next Day refuses to move.
all.suggested_fix: Export one `vehicleCondition(info): 'ok' | 'broken' | 'wrecked'` (pure, from the engine) and use it in both places. Decide once how maxHp 0 is treated, e.g. as unconfigured: no HP rules, plus a separate 'HP not set' warning.
all.rationale: 50: The mismatch is real, and it sits on lines this diff added. src/engine/index.ts:82 `if (v.hp <= 0) return \`${v.name} is wrecked\`` is new in the diff. It has no maxHp guard. The card in src/ui/caravan-app.ts:375-376 does guard with `info.maxHp > 0 &&`. It can trigger. vehicleInfos (src/travel/context.ts:43) returns {hp:0,maxHp:0} when the actor can't be resolved, and pf1Adapter.vehicleHp (src/pf1/index.ts:179-181) returns 0/0 when system.attributes.hp is missing or zero. A PF1 vehicle actor whose HP the GM never entered would hit this: Next Day is blocked with 'Wagon is wrecked' while the card shows 'HP 0/0' with no Wrecked warning. The claim that the sheet 'tells the GM the vehicle is fine' is overstated, though. The same Caravan sheet's SPEED tile (caravan-app.ts:246) shows 'Stopped' and puts pace.blocked ('Wagon is wrecked') in its sub-line, with warn styling. Travel also shows a notification ('The caravan can't move: ...', travel/index.ts:205). So the GM does see why travel stopped; only the per-vehicle card fails to agree. DESIGN.md:210 defines wrecked as '0 HP' and gives no rule for untracked HP, so neither side is clearly the intended behaviour. This is a real but minor consistency or UX bug, and it only shows up with vehicles whose HP isn't set or whose actor is missing.

all.title: `publicRegion` returns neutral rule values that look real, so player previews show DCs that differ from what is rolled
all.description: `partyView` swaps each region for `publicRegion`, which sets `dcMods: {}`, multipliers to 1 and `encounterTable: null`, and drops `map.rules`. The result is still typed `Region`/`MapData`, with nothing to say the values are hidden rather than real. `buildDayContext(party)` feeds that view to `engine.dayPreview` for players (src/travel/context.ts:66), so a player's Travel window in, for example, a +5 Stormlands region shows Navigator DC 18 while the GM's day step rolls against 23. Days-left estimates use multiplier 1 the same way.
all.reason: The type can't tell 'hidden' from 'none', so consumers compute wrong numbers without knowing. That conflicts with ADR-0008's 'published DCs' goal and confuses players at the table.
all.suggested_fix: Mark redacted rules in the type (e.g. `rules: TravelRules | 'hidden'`, or a `redacted: true` flag on the party view). Have the player-side preview omit DCs, or label them 'before region modifiers'. Or decide DC modifiers aren't secret and pass `dcMods` through.
all.rationale:
80: I could not refute this finding; it holds. It is a real bug, this diff exposes it, and it triggers in practice.

- **Where the stripping happens:** `publicRegion` (src/store/index.ts:116) sets `dcMods` to {}, both multipliers to 1 and `encounterTable` to null. `partyView` also builds from `emptyMap()`, so `map.rules` never reaches the player's copy.
- **Where the wrong DCs come from:** `travel.preview()` (src/travel/index.ts:379) calls `engine.dayPreview(buildDayContext())`. For a player, `buildDayContext` defaults to `party = true` and uses `store.partyView` (src/travel/context.ts:66).
- **How the engine uses it:** `buildChecks` reads `rulesFor(map, dcHex).dcMods` (src/engine/index.ts:161-165). With dcMods empty, a player's DCs never include the region modifier.
- **Where players see it:** the Travel window renders `DC ${ch.dc}` under "Today's checks" for every user, with no GM-only branch (src/ui/travel-app.ts:86-92).
- **What the GM rolls against:** the GM's day step uses `buildDayContext(false)`, the full map (src/travel/index.ts:202). In a +5 Stormlands hex the player sees a DC 5 lower than the one rolled. The real DC then appears on the summary card, so players see the two numbers disagree.

**Why hiding the modifier is not the design:** DESIGN §6 says the summary card shows each role's DC and that a DC "hints at its terrain or region modifier; accepted as minor". So players are meant to see true DCs, and the type gives consumers no way to tell "hidden" from "none".

**Is it on a changed line?** Mostly. The stripping inside `publicRegion` already existed at 15741e7 (`dcMods: {}`, `waterMultiplier: 1`); this diff only added `rationsMultiplier: 1`. What is new is the path that feeds the player view into the engine's DC preview: src/travel/context.ts did not exist before, and neither did the player-visible "Today's checks" table. The new diff is what makes this a visible bug.

**Severity:** the effect is display only. Rolls and resolution use GM truth, so nothing is mis-resolved. Wrong DCs on screen are still confusing at the table. I score it 80 rather than higher for those two reasons: the stripping itself predates this diff, and the wrong numbers are only displayed, never rolled.
